articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback, is all set to bounce back on the field after a grueling time in the last few months. The Super Bowl champion has battled doubts about his skills as he spent the majority of his time in recovery. Ahead of the new season, the top quarterback Patrick Mahomes has partnered with a luxury brand.Patrick Mahomes makes an update about his new campaign with Oakley just days ahead of the season opener against Denver BroncosA few hours ago, the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Patrick Mahomes took to his social media to make a post about his new campaign with luxury eyewear brand, Oakley.The clip shows Patrick Mahomes gearing up with a caption that read as, “It’s always showtime. The Patrick Mahomes II Signature Series Permian, available online and in select stores.”Patrick Mahomes signed a contract with luxury eyewear brand, Oakley, in 2019. The contract is worth multi million dollars even though the exact value has not been confirmed yet.In an interview, Patrick Mahomes opened up about the collaboration as he said, “I’m proud to be a part of the Oakley campaign alongside athletes that I’ve watched and admired for years…Hopefully, my story can inspire others to pursue their obsessions and achieve more than they thought possible.”The Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback added, “I’m excited I can just keep building my brand…(I was) able to align myself with a lot of great organizations and partners that understood that football was still the first thing, but I got to go around and see and meet a lot of great people.”Ben Goss, Oakley’s global marketing director, also reflected on signing Patrick Mahomes as he said, “So the partnership with Oakley is a natural fit…He’s a player that relies heavily on his vision to be successful on the football field, and Oakley is a brand that delivers leading optic innovation…”Over the last few years, Patrick Mahomes has been loyal to Oakley and is often spotted wearing them as he arrives at the stadium before changing into the Kansas City Chiefs’ jersey.Patrick Mahomes earns over a whopping $20 million from his brand partnershipsWhile Patrick Mahomes has recently signed a $500 million contract extension with the Kansas City Chiefs, he also earns a pretty hefty amount from his brand partnerships.As per Celebrity Net Worth, the off field deals with luxury brands earns Patrick Mahomes more than $20 million per year.This includes State Farm, Adidas, Coors Light, Subway, Hublot, and Walmart.At this point in time, all eyes remain on the Super Bowl champion as he gears up to make a comeback after sustaining severe injuries in December last year.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I felt let down as a wife and as a mother": Has Gisele Bündchen spoken about why she ended her marriage to Tom Brady?
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, was married to Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bündchen for thirteen years before they ended their marriage.
articles.body: Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, was married to Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bündchen for thirteen years before they ended their marriage in 2022. While it has been a couple of years since their separation, neither Tom Brady nor Gisele Bündchen has spoken about the reason behind it.Has Gisele Bündchen spoken about Tom Brady’s focus on his career leading to their divorce?No, the former Victoria’s Secret model Gisele Bündchen has made no such claims about her marriage to the New England Patriots’ legend Tom Brady.A fanpage on X made a fake post that read as, “Gisele Bündchen reportedly opened up about the reasons behind the end of her marriage to Tom Brady, making several explosive claims about their relationship and family life. According to the statement, Gisele felt that Tom was often absent and failed to give their family the attention she believed they deserved.”The post added, “”I felt let down as a wife and as a mother watching everything unfold.” She also addressed accusations of infidelity and the difficult moments in their relationship, saying that resentment and regret eventually consumed their marriage. According to the claims, Gisele eventually gave Tom an ultimatum, asking him to prioritize either his family or his football career. “He made it clear that he had built his career long before I came into his life and that he wasn’t prepared to walk away from it, even for his family. That was when I realized I had to make a decision for myself.””The post is entirely fake as Gisele Bündchen has made no such claims about her divorce to Tom Brady.Months after their divorce, Gisele Bündchen sat for an interview with Vogue where she said the reason behind their divorce is not so “black and white”.Despite the post on X being fake, it has sparked a heated debate among fans.A fan took to X and wrote, “She finally said what a lot of people already knew. He built his whole identity around football, she built hers around the family they actually had, and when she asked him to choose, he chose the game.”Another fan posted, “That sounds like years of hurt and resentment building up. 💔 No matter how successful someone is, being present for your family matters too. Sometimes love alone isn’t enough when two people want different things from life.A third fan posted, “She’s called the ultimatum story hurtful rumor, said the split was more complicated than football vs. family, and that she has no regrets and still wants Tom to be happy.”Another fan noted, “This is recycled fake news. Gisele has already addressed these exact claims years ago and denied giving any ultimatum. She described the split as them growing apart, not this dramatic version. Same fabricated quotes keep getting reposted for engagement.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ $218 million Alpine F1 investment gets a major luxury boost with Gucci partnership
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has plenty on his plate as the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for another NFL season, but the superstar quarterback is also watching devel.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has plenty on his plate as the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for another NFL season, but the superstar quarterback is also watching developments far beyond the football field. One of his biggest sports investments is entering a fresh chapter, and Mahomes appeared to welcome the change with a simple but telling reaction on social media.Patrick Mahomes Reacts To Alpine F1’s Gucci MoveMahomes and Chiefs teammate Travis Kelce are not just casual Formula 1 fans. The two NFL stars became investors in the Alpine F1 team in 2022, joining a group of high-profile backers looking to help the racing operation grow its global profile.Now, Alpine is preparing for a major identity shift.Formula 1 has reported that Gucci will become Alpine’s title partner in 2027. The partnership is expected to bring a new visual identity to the team, including Gucci-inspired colors and a new racing banner.For Mahomes, the announcement seems to have landed well.The Chiefs quarterback responded to the news on Twitter with several flame emojis. It was a brief reaction, but given his interest in fashion and his connection to Alpine, the response was hardly surprising.The Gucci partnership also adds another layer to an investment that could become increasingly valuable as Alpine works to rebuild its standing in Formula 1.Alpine F1’s Turnaround Could Give Mahomes More To CelebrateThe timing of the announcement is particularly interesting because Alpine has been trying to change its fortunes on the track.The team endured a difficult 2025 season and ended the campaign at the bottom of the Formula 1 standings. Rather than allowing that result to dictate its next move, Alpine shifted its focus toward the following car earlier than usual.That decision appears to be paying off.Five races into the 2026 season, Alpine has moved into fifth place in the constructors' standings, putting it ahead of the rest of the midfield while trailing Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull.That progress matters for Mahomes and Kelce as investors. Formula 1 is no longer simply a racing competition. Team value, sponsorship power, international reach and brand appeal all play a major role in the business surrounding the sport.Alpine's relationship with Mercedes is also evolving. Mercedes was linked with a possible ownership move involving Alpine, but that deal did not materialize. Mercedes will, however, remain involved as Alpine's engine and powertrain supplier.For Mahomes, the latest developments offer a fascinating mix of sport, business and fashion. His NFL career remains the headline act, but his growing portfolio continues to take him into unexpected territory.And if Alpine can keep climbing the Formula 1 standings while adding a luxury powerhouse such as Gucci to its name, Mahomes may have even more reasons to keep watching closely.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ health becomes focus as Chiefs QB recovers from knee injury ahead of 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: NFL News: US President had one question on his mind when he met the owner of a Kansas City barbecue restaurant at the White House: how Patrick Mahomes was doing.
articles.body: US President had one question on his mind when he met the owner of a Kansas City barbecue restaurant at the White House: how Patrick Mahomes was doing. Trump spoke with Joe Pearce, co-owner of Slap’s BBQ, during the White House Small Business Summit on May 4, 2026. The conversation quickly moved from business to football as Trump asked about the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback’s recovery from his knee injury. Pearce told him Mahomes was doing well, while Trump then asked whether the quarterback could be ready for the start of the 2026 NFL season.US President asks Joe Pearce about Patrick Mahomes’ recoveryPresident began the conversation by asking Pearce about Mahomes’ condition.“The most important thing, how’s Mahomes doing?” Trump asked. “Is he OK?”Pearce, who co-owns Slap’s BBQ with his brother Mike Pearce, replied that Mahomes was OK.Trump then made it clear that he wanted the quarterback to return soon.“You tell the people we love him,” Trump said.The president did not stop there. He asked Pearce whether Mahomes would be able to start the first game of the 2026 season.“So, he’ll start Game 1, you think?”Pearce and his brother responded that they were hopeful. When Trump asked if Mahomes would at least be close to returning, Pearce again gave an optimistic answer.“Real close, real close,” he said.Trump also asked whether Pearce knew Mahomes personally. Pearce explained that Mahomes and people around the Chiefs had ordered from his restaurant from time to time.Trump then asked Pearce to pass along his best wishes.“You let him know, I want him to get better fast, I hope he plays the whole season,” Trump said.Patrick Mahomes continues recovery from knee injuryMahomes is recovering from a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. He suffered the injury during the Chiefs’ 2025 season and has been working through his rehabilitation ahead of the new campaign.There have been encouraging signs in his recovery. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid recently said Mahomes was throwing the football and doing his training work without problems.“Yeah, I know he’s doing a lot of stuff right now,” Reid said.Chiefs general manager Brett Veach has also offered an upbeat update, saying Mahomes was “way ahead of schedule” in his recovery.Still, Pearce could only offer hope when Trump asked about Mahomes starting the season. His comments were not an official medical update from the Chiefs.The exchange showed how closely Mahomes’ recovery is being followed, even outside the team and the NFL. Trump used his meeting with a Kansas City business owner to ask about one of the city’s biggest sports stars, before returning to the business summit.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “If I take this job then I will have more money to invest in this..”: Why Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced questions over their donations despite their $700 million fortune
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen built huge fortunes during their marriage, but their charitable work also faced scrutiny. In Nov. 2022, public records s.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen built huge fortunes during their marriage, but their charitable work also faced scrutiny. In Nov. 2022, public records showed that the Luz Foundation had given $640,402 to various organisations between 2007 and 2019. That figure drew attention because the former couple’s combined wealth was estimated at more than $700 million at the time. Their foundation’s spending soon became a talking point around their philanthropy.The criticism did not mean the couple made no charitable contributions. Brady and Bündchen had supported hunger relief, environmental causes and other organisations for years. Bündchen also continued developing her own philanthropic work, and the Luz Alliance Fund later became involved in much larger fundraising campaigns across Brazil.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced scrutiny over the Luz Foundation’s donationsThe Luz Foundation began in 2007 after Bündchen created it to support educational, environmental and humanitarian causes. Brady later shared leadership of the organisation with Peter Mattoon, who also worked with Brady on his investments and business activities.According to the financial records reported by EL PAÍS on Nov. 23, 2022, the foundation donated $640,402 between 2007 and 2019. Some of the individual payments attracted attention because of their size. The foundation gave $300 to an environmental organisation in Costa Rica in 2018. It also donated $1,000 to the Challenged Athletes Foundation and $900 to the World Wildlife Fund.Several larger donations went to organisations focused on meditation and yoga. The Luz Foundation gave $80,000 to the Pointing Out the Great Way Foundation in 2019. It also donated $25,000 to the David Lynch Foundation and another $25,000 to the You Go Girl Yoga Foundation.The foundation also supported environmental work connected to Bündchen’s interests. It gave $48,000 to the Alliance for Forests in 2014 and $25,000 the following year. The organisation works on forests, biodiversity, climate and rural communities.Bündchen had already spoken about the link between her career and philanthropy. In a 2015 interview with the “Sydney Morning Herald”, she explained why she continued working as a model while putting money into causes she supported.“I know what people think: ‘This girl is only posing for the pictures’,” Bündchen said in the interview.She then explained her reasoning: “If I take this job then I will have more money to invest in this project. So that’s what I’m doing.”The comments gave some context to how Bündchen viewed her modelling income. Her charitable work also extended beyond the Luz Foundation. She had supported environmental programmes, humanitarian projects and disaster relief through different partnerships over the years. Gisele Bündchen’s Luz Alliance Fund grew after the criticismIn 2020, Bündchen created the Luz Alliance Fund with BrazilFoundation. The fund initially focused on helping Brazilian families affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. It later expanded into environmental protection, regeneration and emergency relief.Bündchen and Brady also stepped up during the pandemic in the United States. In 2020, the couple donated 750,000 meals through a partnership with Feeding Tampa Bay. Brady separately joined the broader Meals Up campaign, which helped raise millions of meals for Feeding America. Recent reporting says Brady’s wider efforts helped unlock significant funding for hunger-relief organisations during the pandemic.Bündchen’s biggest recent fundraising effort came after the devastating floods in Rio Grande do Sul in May 2024. The Brazilian state suffered widespread destruction, and Bündchen used the Luz Alliance Fund to encourage donations and support relief organisations.BrazilFoundation later reported that the campaign raised close to $3 million through thousands of individual and corporate donations. The money supported emergency relief and rebuilding work. The organisation’s 2024 annual report says the Luz Alliance Fund supported 21 organisations responding to the disaster.The campaign also showed how Bündchen’s charitable platform had expanded beyond the smaller foundation payments that attracted criticism. Her public profile helped bring international attention to the disaster and encouraged people to contribute to relief efforts.Brady has continued his own charitable work separately through the Change the World Foundation. Public nonprofit records show that the foundation reported charitable disbursements in its latest available filings.For Brady and Bündchen, philanthropy now covers several different initiatives rather than one foundation alone. Bündchen has focused heavily on Brazil, environmental protection and disaster relief through the Luz Alliance Fund, while Brady continues to support charitable causes through his own foundation and wider partnerships.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Matthew Stafford faces $1.25M tax shock after Rams’ Australia trip puts his Week 1 earnings under scrutiny
articles.summary: NFL News: Matthew Stafford could be in line for a massive tax hit from the Los Angeles Rams’ historic Week 1 trip to Australia. A viral post claims that roughly.
articles.body: Matthew Stafford could be in line for a massive tax hit from the Los Angeles Rams’ historic Week 1 trip to Australia. A viral post claims that roughly $1.25 million of his estimated $2.2 million income from the game could go toward taxes, potentially leaving the Rams quarterback with around $947,000 from that paycheck.The figure adds an intriguing financial angle to a game that already carries plenty of significance, as the Rams prepare to face the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11 in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia, giving Stafford and his teammates a very different opening week from the usual NFL routine.Matthew Stafford’s Australia game could cost him nearly $1.25 million in taxesAccording to the MLFootball post, Australian taxes could account for approximately $960,000 of Stafford’s estimated $2.2 million Week 1 income, while the calculation also puts his federal tax obligation at around $814,000 and California taxes at roughly $293,000, with a foreign tax credit potentially reducing part of the U.S. federal amount.If that estimate comes close to the final calculation, Stafford would keep approximately $947,000 from the $2.2 million figure, meaning almost 57% of the estimated income could disappear through taxes, although the number circulating online comes from the MLFootball post rather than a confirmed tax assessment.The unusual tax situation comes from an equally unusual NFL assignment, because the Rams are traveling more than 9,000 miles from Los Angeles to Melbourne for a game that will put the league on a completely new stage. The matchup also gives the Rams the home-team designation, while the 49ers will technically play the road side despite having arrived in Australia earlier to give their players more time to adjust to the 14-hour time difference.Los Angeles has taken a different approach by planning to arrive much closer to the game, with the organization trying to keep the week as normal as possible for its players despite the enormous journey. The football operation itself has required months of planning, with the Rams moving roughly 25,000 pounds of equipment that includes helmets, shoulder pads, cleats, different types of spikes, jackets and other supplies.Australia’s strict biosecurity regulations have created another headache, forcing the Rams to make sure their equipment arrives clean and free from soil, grass and seeds, while several drinks, supplements and other game-day products had to reach Melbourne months before the team because the organization could not simply carry all of those items into the country.The Rams also have more than football on their plate because Los Angeles received Australia through the NFL’s Global Markets Program, which gives selected teams international marketing rights and requires the organization to promote its brand while helping grow the sport in the country. Matthew Stafford also has a separate $534K California tax issueThe Australia tax claim comes with another significant tax story surrounding Stafford and his wife, Kelly, although the two matters remain separate.On July 14, the California Franchise Tax Board filed a $534,453.67 tax lien against the couple for the 2024 taxable year, according to Page Six, while Los Angeles County officials confirmed that the lien remained active when the publication reported the matter on August 11.The lien relates to property and property rights owned by the Staffords or potentially acquired by them, which draws attention given the couple’s sizeable real estate portfolio in Hidden Hills. They purchased a mansion for $10.5 million in 2022 before buying the neighboring property for $28.15 million in 2023, while three other Hidden Hills homes connected to the couple later sold for a combined $21.3 million.All of that comes against the backdrop of Stafford’s new one-year, $55 million contract with the Rams, which followed his MVP season and kept the veteran quarterback in Los Angeles after questions had surrounded his future in the NFL.Now, Stafford heads into the Australia opener with the Rams facing the 49ers in a game that will make league history, while an estimated $1.25 million tax hit adds another unusual layer to what is already one of the most talked-about Week 1 matchups of the 2026 season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes went from a torn ACL and LCL to week 1 starter in just 9 months and why nobody should be surprised
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL in his left knee on December 14, 2025, in a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. Surgery followed within 24 hours. T.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL in his left knee on December 14, 2025, in a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. Surgery followed within 24 hours. The Chiefs missed the playoffs for the first time since Mahomes took over as starter. For most quarterbacks, that sequence ends with a long, uncertain road back. For Mahomes, it became a nine-month project with one fixed destination in mind -- Monday Night Football against the Denver Broncos. Andy Reid confirmed it Tuesday: "Pretty good chance Patrick will go ahead and start, unless something were to come up here in the next couple days. But, most likely, he'll be the guy that's out there."How did Patrick Mahomes recover from a torn ACL and LCL so fast?The honest medical answer is that he didn't heal faster. He just got back to performance faster -- and there's a real difference between those two things.Rick Burkholder, the Chiefs' vice president of sports medicine and performance, addressed this directly after the surgery. "He's so regimented in what he does. He's in here at 6 a.m. He's the last guy out at night. He'll take the rehab like that. When you add up all the little things, that allows the player to get back faster. They don't heal up faster, they just get back to performance faster."Standard recovery for a combined ACL and LCL tear typically runs 12 to 18 months. Mahomes is doing it in nine. The surgery, performed by Dr. Dan Cooper in Dallas, confirmed no artery damage, no nerve damage, no meniscal damage. The injury was serious. The variables around it were as favorable as they could be. By March, just 100 days post-surgery, he was already posting throwing videos. By May, he was at OTAs. By mandatory minicamp in June, he was doing everything except 11-on-11 work. When training camp opened in late July, the Chiefs cleared him for full participation."I remember sitting on the table and watching us play those last few games, how much it hurt me," Mahomes said. "But I knew that if I continued to work I could be at this spot where I can get cleared for practice."He hasn't missed a single rep since.Did Mahomes actually look like himself in training camp?That was the real question all summer -- not whether he'd be cleared, but whether he'd look right. The answer, according to everyone who watched him work, was yes.Reid's assessment was blunt. "You guys have seen him out there, so you know what it looks like, him running around and doing his stuff. Other than having a brace on his leg, everything looks normal. He's running around the same way he's always done and throwing the ball like he's always done."Wide receiver Xavier Worthy put it even simpler: "Oh, he's back."Mahomes took every first-team rep throughout camp. He sat out the preseason entirely — a deliberate decision by the franchise to protect him and keep the knee fresh heading into September. The lack of preseason action raised eyebrows, but Mahomes had already accounted for that. "You just have to build that confidence back," he said in late July. "I didn't want to have to get only a couple of weeks of practice in and then have to go play a game. I wanted to build it up, see how training camp goes as we gradually build."That is not a man managing fear. That is a man managing a plan.What does Mahomes' return mean for the Chiefs and the 2026 season?Kansas City went 6-11 last season without him. The offense stalled, the playoffs were missed for the first time in the Mahomes era, and the conversation around the Chiefs shifted from dynasty to question mark. That changes Monday night. Mahomes returning to the starting lineup against Denver isn't just a feel-good moment -- it resets every projection about this team.The Chiefs signed running back Kenneth Walker in the offseason, Eric Bieniemy is back running an offense that produced Mahomes' best football, and the roster has been rebuilt around a quarterback who is, by his own admission, already thinking beyond Week 1. "The process isn't over," he told reporters at training camp. "It'll be something I'll probably be dealing with the next few years of my career and throughout the rest of my career." Then he added: "I feel amazing. I'm excited just to be able to play football."Mahomes is also the clear early frontrunner for Comeback Player of the Year -- before he has played a single snap. And his contract, recently extended through 2033 at a total value of $504.75 million, signals exactly where the Chiefs stand on their investment in him. He also comes in as the consensus pick for best quarterback in the NFL, according to the latest poll of coaches, GMs and executives by Albert Breer. Nine months removed from a destroyed knee, that is where Mahomes sits.Nobody who has watched him this offseason should be surprised.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 49ers lose DT Alfred Collins for the season with knee injury ahead of Rams opener in Australia
articles.summary: Alfred Collins went down with a knee injury in Melbourne on Tuesday, and will now miss all of his second season in the league.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers will be without a key piece to their defensive front this season after all.

Alfred Collins will miss the entire 2026 campaign after he went down with a torn patellar tendon in his knee this week in Melbourne, head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed on Wednesday. Specifics of the injury aren't yet known, but he is now done for the year.

The 49ers selected Collins with the No. 43 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Texas, and he had a solid rookie campaign rotating through the defensive line. He had 17 total tackles and a sack, and recovered two fumbles, during his first season in the league.

Collins made quite the impression on his former defensive coordinator, too.

"Alfred, I know he was a second-round pick and all, but he's still probably the biggest surprise to me in terms of just how much better he got from training camp," Robert Saleh, now the head coach in Tennessee , told NBC Sports Bay Area in June . "As the season went on, I think he's going to be special. His mindset to get better, his work ethic, he's only going to get better. And when it triggers for him, he's going to be a bear to stop."

It's unclear who the 49ers will bring in to replace Collins, but they have both defensive tackles Kevin Givens and Sebastian Valdez on the practice squad available.

The 49ers will open the 2026 NFL season against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night in Melbourne, Australia. It marks the first regular-season NFL game to be played in the country. The 49ers made the trek over last week for an extended stay, while the Rams left on Tuesday night and will be in the country for only roughly three days.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers drops a bombshell: NFL teams deliberately cut veterans to dodge guaranteed contract payouts
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers is not holding back anymore. On the \"Not Just Football\" podcast this week, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback called out one of the NFL.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is not holding back anymore. On the "Not Just Football" podcast this week, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback called out one of the NFL's most quietly damaging practices -- teams releasing veteran players right before the season opens, only to re-sign them afterward, all to avoid triggering guaranteed contract money. Rodgers did not frame this as a complaint. He framed it as a structural flaw that the league has been glossing over for years while experienced players silently pay the price.Why do NFL teams cut veteran players before the season starts?The answer, according to Aaron Rodgers, is money -- and a very specific rule that most fans never think about.Under the current collective bargaining agreement, a player's contract becomes fully guaranteed if he is on the 53-man roster on the first day of the regular season. That one clause has quietly reshaped how franchises handle their older players. Teams know the window. So they cut veterans before that date hits, wait for the roster dust to settle, then bring those same players back once the financial obligation resets."The older players have been less and less respected as the years have gone on," Rodgers said. "The NFL is not a meritocracy, not purely a meritocracy. And there are weird things around the contracts where veteran contracts, if you're on the 53 the first day of the season, your contract's guaranteed. So, a lot of teams now will cut veteran players and then bring them back, you know, after the first day of the league year begins, which I think is a really weird part of it."It is, frankly, a loophole hiding in plain sight. And what makes it worse is that the players most affected by it are precisely those who have given years of service to the league. They get released, sit in uncertainty for days, and then get a call asking them to return under terms the team now controls more tightly. That is not how a league that talks endlessly about player welfare should operate.The practice squad has improved -- Rodgers acknowledged that -- and older players can now hold spots there in ways that were not possible when he entered the league. But that is a minor concession against a much broader structural problem.Do NFL teams prioritize draft picks over better veteran players?This was the second edge to Rodgers' argument, and arguably the sharper one.He pointed out that franchises frequently protect roster spots for draft picks who have not earned them, simply because of the round in which they were selected. A third-round pick sits on the 53-man roster while a more deserving veteran on the practice squad gets the call to actually play on game day."Obviously, draft picks are valued more than others in certain places," Rodgers said. articles.title: Aaron Donald’s alleged private texts with his ex come to light in court as the NFL legend faces a custody battle involving their children
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Donald’s alleged private texts with his former partner, Jaelynn Blakey, have surfaced as part of a court dispute involving their children and a .
articles.body: Aaron Donald’s alleged private texts with his former partner, Jaelynn Blakey, have surfaced as part of a court dispute involving their children and a French bulldog. The former couple disagreed over whether the dog posed a risk to their kids, with Donald seeking court action after claiming the animal had bitten family members. Blakey disputed his account and defended keeping the dog, saying it had been part of the family for years. The dispute eventually ended with the dog being permanently removed from her home.The court fight has added a personal wrinkle to a major period in Donald’s life. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year retired from the NFL in 2024 but is now preparing for a return with the Los Angeles Rams. While his football comeback has drawn plenty of attention, documents from his custody dispute have brought his family life into focus as well.Aaron Donald’s alleged private texts with ex revealed in custody battleThe dispute centered on Aaron Donald’s concerns about the French bulldog living at Blakey’s Los Angeles home. According to court documents, Donald claimed the dog had bitten their daughter on the mouth in September 2023. He also said Blakey’s niece was bitten less than a year later and alleged their son was bitten in the face in March 2026.Donald said Blakey had agreed after each incident to remove the dog. He later claimed the animal had returned to the home without his knowledge and that their children told him about its return.In one message obtained by TMZ, Donald wrote, "But on another note don't fill comfortable with kids in that house with that dog. It bit 3 people in the face and 2 of those people was Jaeda and AJ."He followed with another message, saying, "You said you got read [sic] of the dog and it keep popping back up not really understand the disconnect with that."Donald also wrote, "There's multiple different places you can put the dog; it's just not stable having that dog around no kids because it got a history of bitting , it already happened multiple times."He accused Blakey of telling the children not to tell him the dog was back at the house.Blakey pushed back strongly against those claims in an email dated July 2, 2026. She denied hiding the dog and questioned why she would need to tell the children to conceal its presence."Why would I tell my children that when the dog moves freely and talk with their father daily at my home, and he can see for himself?"She added, "You have no proof of that, so let's not even start making accusations ... I would never tell them that. I told Mr. Donald at the time of the incident the dog was removed ... and he was. Your claims are ridiculous."Blakey also denied agreeing to permanently remove the dog. She said the children were not afraid of the animal and described it as an important part of their home.What happened between Aaron Donald and Jaelynn Blakey?Donald and Blakey never married. They separated around the time Donald and the Rams moved from St. Louis to Los Angeles in 2016.The former couple shares two children, daughter Jaeda and son Aaron Jr. Donald later asked for sole physical custody of the children until Blakey removed the dog, according to the court documents.Blakey argued the animal was not dangerous and said Donald was trying to force her to give up a pet she had relied on during difficult periods.Aaron Donald is happily married to Erica DonaldDonald later married Erica Donald, and the couple has two children together. Erica has also been closely involved in his career and business interests.She worked with the Rams in community affairs and player involvement before moving into sports marketing. She later worked with Game1 and Donda Sports, where Aaron also had a partnership.When Donald announced his return to the Rams, Erica joked on X, "I let him out [of] the house y’all 🤣💙🫶🏽," after he signed a one-year, $20 million deal on Aug. 30.Their family now includes their two children together and Donald’s two children from his previous relationship.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New coach, new defense, high expectations for Bills in power rankings
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Bills are right where they always rank as the 2026 NFL season gets underway.
articles.body:
Two hundred and thirty-nine days. That's how long Buffalo Bills fans have waited for meaningful football to return.

When the Bills lost to the Denver Broncos in overtime, 33-30, on Jan. 17, during an AFC divisional playoff game, it triggered a cascade of changes in Orchard Park. Here's the short list:

Head coach Sean McDermott and nearly the entire coaching staff were fired.

Offensive coordinator Joe Brady was hired as head coach.

The defense was switched from a hybrid 4-3 to a 3-4, with Jim Leonhard brought in to oversee it.

The team ultimately opted to trade out of the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

The Bills traded for a veteran agent wide receiver ( D.J. Moore ) for Josh Allen .

Oh, and the Bills opened their new $2.2 billion stadium.

Surprisingly, after all that tumult, Buffalo is pretty much where it's always been in the power rankings: a top-five team.

As the Bills prepare to open their season on the road against the Houston Texans , Buffalo's average power ranking is 3.5. The median is also 3.5.

Bills: New coach Joe Brady will bring a much more aggressive approach to this team. That's something that is badly needed.

Texans: We know the defense will be dominant, so it's all about the offense. More specifically, it's about C.J. Stroud . He has to be better.

Bills projected win total: 10.8. The defense is undergoing a significant change, entering a 3-4 scheme with six new starters, and that's part of the reason for hope. The other is a fresh start with coach Joe Brady that could get this team over the hump and into the Super Bowl. Even if last season didn't go as planned, it's hard to keep a Josh Allen-led team out of the top five entering the season.

Texans projected win total: 9.3. There's no defensive line in the NFL more feared than the Texans', which boasts an embarrassment of riches after adding Jadeveon Clowney to a group that already featured Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter . So we know the defense should be very good. The big question is what can C.J. Stroud do in Year 4 after his 2025 campaign ended with a terrible playoff performance. They may have to win games 17-14.

Bills: There isn't a team east of Los Angeles more in Super Bowl-or-bust mode than the Buffalo Bills .

The Bills dismissed their highly successful coach because he couldn't get the team over the hump. They are led by Josh Allen, who has more playoff wins than any quarterback in NFL history without a Super Bowl appearance.

The good news is the team should be in the thick of it in the AFC. The offense has the league's reigning rushing king and a new No. 1 wide receiver in D.J. Moore . The defense ranked seventh in the league last year.

The bad news is that the Bills have been in the thick of it for the better part of a decade, but for whatever reason they come up short in the postseason. — Gary Davenport

Texans: The Houston Texans will go as far as quarterback C.J. Stroud takes them. He doesn't need to operate at any MVP standard for the Texans to become a serious Super Bowl contender, either.

Houston 's defense is already good enough to place the team among the NFL's best. The quarterback simply needs to be better than what's been seen the last two seasons and closer to how he performed as a rookie.

The pieces are now around him after the acquisition of running back David Montgomery and the front office reworking the offensive line.

For most NFL teams, the idea of playing complementary football is getting enough from a defense to ensure the squad's high-flying offense doesn't find itself in a shootout every week. In Houston's case, its defense dictates terms.

However, the Texans need to consistently move the ball offensively. If Stroud and Co. do so, the AFC will be ripe for the taking. — Brent Sobleski

Bills' odds of making the playoffs/winning Super Bowl: 77%/8%.

For the first time since 2017, the Bills will have a leader other than Sean McDermott — but promoting former offensive coordinator Joe Brady to head coach should retain Buffalo's hyper-efficient offense with Josh Allen and James Cook . All eyes are on Jim Leonhard as the Bills' new defensive coordinator, looking to round out a unit with question marks but talent at all three levels. Buffalo enters the season with the highest division odds (56%) of any team, with a weaker AFC East making the Bills seem like a near-playoff lock for the eighth straight season.

Texans' odds of making the playoffs/winning Super Bowl: 66%/5%

Houston's defense was one of the most defining units of the entire 2025 season, and the group looks extremely stout yet again with Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr. , Jalen Pitre , Kamari Lassiter and many more. Houston's offense — especially quarterback C.J. Stroud — looks to perform better after a playoff flameout, with the addition of David Montgomery and an updated offensive line changing the equation. DeMeco Ryans ' defense sets a high floor for Houston, although the team's ceiling will ultimately be dictated by what the other side of the ball can achieve after placing 27th in explosive play rate last year.

Stock up, stock down on 6 Bills heading into the first preseason game

Bills: The feel-good vibes in Western New York are hard to ignore, even amid all the changes for what's become a perennial AFC power … and, perhaps for the first time in more than three decades, the AFC's preeminent force.

Texans : A defense that ceded more than 300 yards just six times last year might need to be even better until QB C.J. Stroud and an offense already coping with significant injuries can find its footing. But that could be a tall order given some of the high-powered attacks the Texans will face in the next two months.

Chances to make the playoffs: 84.1% Chances to win division: 67.1% Projected wins: 10.7 Strength of schedule: 14th easiest 2025 record: 12-5

Bills' biggest strength: Josh Allen. It's pretty simple. The Bills have an opportunity to win a Super Bowl once again this year, despite a first-time head coach, and that's because of who is playing quarterback. Allen, 30, is going into his ninth NFL season and has a new No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore. Breaking records has become commonplace for the 2024 MVP, and Allen gives the team a chance in every game. -- Alaina Getzenberg

Biggest concern: It is a transition year for the new defensive scheme. Coordinator Jim Leonhard has been open about the fact this year's defense will not fully look like his vision for the unit as it transitions from a 4-3 to 3-4 base. There is a mix of new players who fit the scheme specifically and carryovers from the previous regime. How the group comes together will go a long way in determining the unit's success. -- Getzenberg

QB stat to know: Allen's dual-threat ability is unlike anything the NFL has seen. Allen already has 299 passing and rushing TDs combined in his first eight seasons, 40 more than the next-closest player ( Patrick Mahomes , 259). In fact, he already has the most through a player's first nine seasons (next closest: Peyton Manning , 288). -- ESPN Research

Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 13-4 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 8-9

This season is a success if ... the Bills reach the Super Bowl. Unfortunately for new coach Joe Brady, that's the bar. Maximizing Allen's tenure is the priority, and anything comparable to or less than what Sean McDermott accomplished won't make for a fully successful season. -- Getzenberg

One key fantasy nugget: Allen gives fantasy managers a major boost when the Bills have the ball on the doorstep of the end zone. He converted 22 of 28 true goal-line carries (78.6%) over the past three seasons. -- Matt Bowen

Bold prediction for 2026: Wide receiver Keon Coleman will record 750 or more receiving yards and at least five touchdowns -- both career highs. Earlier this offseason I thought there was a decent chance he'd be on a different team by now. But Coleman also hasn't been that bad in his first two years, posting a 49 overall score in ESPN's receiver score (just below average) and 1.6 yards per route run. Even though the Bills added Moore, I could see Coleman having a mini breakout in Year 3. -- Seth Walder

Out of thousands, these Bills Camp photos made the cut for Shawn Dowd

Chances to make the playoffs: 58.9% Chances to win division: 40.5% Projected wins: 9.3 Strength of schedule: 10th hardest 2025 record: 12-5

Biggest strength: How could it be anything but Houston's defense? It's arguably the best in the NFL, and it brought back nine of 11 starters. The unit holds three All-Pros in cornerback Derek Stingley Jr., to pair with their defensive end duo of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter. There are also three other Pro Bowlers on the unit with linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair , safety Calen Bullock and cornerback Kamari Lassiter. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Biggest concern: Well the general consensus would be quarterback C.J. Stroud, but in reality it's the people protecting Stroud. When he's protected, he has produced a QBR of 66 in his career (15th since 2023), but when he's under pressure, it drops to 27. If the offensive line can protect him, that also means the run game should be effective. There are potentially two new starters on the unit in center Evan Brown and rookie guard Keylan Rutledge. -- Bien-Aime

QB stat to know: After one of the best rookie seasons in NFL history in 2023, Stroud has struggled to replicate that success in the following two seasons -- due in part to having one of the worst offensive line units last season, ranking last in run block win rate (68%) and 30th in pass block win rate (56%). In 2023 Houston ranked 25th in RBWR (70%) and 10th in PBWR (61%). -- ESPN Research

Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 12-5 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 7-10

This season is a success if ... Stroud looks like what people thought he would become after his historic rookie season. The Texans have Super Bowl aspirations, and that could put them in line to raise the Lombardi Trophy. -- Bien-Aime

One key fantasy nugget: To improve their run game, the Texans traded for running back David Montgomery and upgraded the offensive line. Montgomery, who has 33 rushing scores over his past three seasons, will get plenty of looks when Houston moves the ball into the red zone. -- Bowen

Bold prediction for 2026: Wide receiver Nico Collins will record 1,500 receiving yards. With Jayden Higgins out for the year, Collins should earn an even higher share of targets (even following the Kayshon Boutte trade). Collins is already a great receiver, perhaps in the second tier behind the true elites like Ja'Marr Chase, Puka Nacua , Justin Jefferson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba . But I wonder if we'll be talking about Collins in that group at the end of this season. -- Walder

articles.title: NFL 2026 schedule & key fixtures: Start date, play-offs, Super Bowl 61 & Christmas games
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL season set to start on Wednesday, here are all the key dates and fixtures on the road to Super Bowl 61.
articles.body:
The new NFL season begins this week and if the pressure is on defending champions Seattle, they are not showing it.

The Seahawks' defence dominated the New England Patriots to win the Super Bowl for a second time in February.

And British coach Aden Durde, who remains Seattle's defensive coordinator, is ready to go again after becoming the first overseas coach to win the NFL's biggest prize.

"It's an experience that was unreal," he told BBC Sport. "It's hard to explain but, for myself, I felt it gave me an overview of why I really enjoy what I do and why I do it.

"It's the thirst for the process and for improvement, doing it on a day-to-day basis. Now we get another chance to do that and that's the exciting thing."

Seattle begin their title defence with a Super Bowl rematch against the Patriots on Wednesday (01:20 BST, Thursday).

But their biggest threat is set to be the Los Angeles Rams, who are favourites to win Super Bowl 61 after bolstering their star-studded roster.

Last year the divisional rivals produced two thrilling games in the regular season before Seattle edged out the Rams in a play-off classic.

"Who knows what [that rivalry] will look like this year," added Durde. "That's the whole point of the off-season, the work we've put in to sharpen ourselves and get ourselves battle ready."

Now it's time to let battle commence - so here's a rundown of this season's key fixtures.

Since 2004, the opening game of the NFL season has featured the defending champions.

Seattle triumphed in Santa Clara in February so will host this year's kick-off game and it will be the first season opener to feature a Super Bowl rematch since 2016.

The NFL season normally starts on a Thursday, and in the past two years the season's first international game has been played on a Friday.

However, the NFL's 2026 schedule is starting a week later than normal, bringing it into conflict with US bylaws which prohibit professional American football games being broadcast on a Friday or Saturday from the second week of September.

So the Rams' game against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, in front of 100,000 fans at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground, will kick off at 10:35 local time on Friday, which will be Thursday evening in the US (01:35 BST, Friday).

The season opener has therefore been brought forward to a Wednesday for the first time since 2012.

Next Thursday will mark the first game at the Buffalo Bills' new home, with the Detroit Lions heading to Highmark Stadium, while on 25 October the Super Bowl's Most Valuable Player Kenneth Walker makes a swift return to Seattle after joining the Kansas City Chiefs.

What are the Thanksgiving and Christmas games?

American football is a big part of the holidays in the US and Thanksgiving week now features five games while there is again a triple-header on Christmas Day.

The NFL will play its first game on Thanksgiving Eve as the Rams, who feature in a league-high seven prime-time games, host the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, 25 November.

That's followed by a Thanksgiving triple-header on Thursday, 26 November, which begins with two divisional match-ups as Detroit host the Chicago Bears (18:00 GMT) and the Dallas Cowboys welcome the Philadelphia Eagles (21:25 GMT).

Then provided Patrick Mahomes makes a smooth return from injury, the star quarterback will renew his rivalry with Josh Allen as Kansas City visit Buffalo (01:20 GMT Friday).

For the fourth straight year, the Thanksgiving slate concludes with a Black Friday clash on 27 November as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Denver Broncos.

That is one of 17 games to be streamed on Amazon Prime, which include the Houston Texans at Philadelphia on Christmas Eve, plus the Baltimore Ravens at the Cincinnati Bengals on New Year's Eve.

Netflix will stream five games, including two on Christmas Day, when Chicago host divisional rivals Green Bay (18:00 GMT) before Denver welcome Buffalo (21:30 GMT).

The festive triple-header concludes with a repeat of last season's epic NFC Championship game, as Seattle host the Rams (01:15 GMT, 26 December).

After a record seven international games last year, there will be nine during the 2026 season, with Australia and France becoming hosts for the first time.

Regular season games will be played across four continents and seven countries, with the NFL returning to Mexico after a four-year gap while Brazil, Germany, Spain and the UK remain on the schedule.

The NFL's regular season ends on Sunday, 10 January 2027, with the play-offs scheduled to begin on 16 January.

They will culminate with Super Bowl 61 on Sunday, 14 February 2027. It will be the first time that the NFL's championship decider is played on Valentine's Day - and the following day is a national holiday in the US, Presidents' Day.

The big game will be held at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, making it the ninth Super Bowl to be played in the Greater Los Angeles area.

Built at a cost of $5.5bn and opened in 2020, it is the world's most expensive stadium and is shared by the Los Angeles Chargers and Rams.

Knowing the Super Bowl would be held in their own stadium in 2022, the Rams went all-in to build a star-studded roster for that season and the gamble paid off as the Rams beat the Cincinnati Bengals 23–20 in front of 70,048.

The Rams have tried to replicate that formula by trading for defensive stars Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie in the off-season while three-time defensive player of the year Aaron Donald, 35, came out of retirement on a one-year deal.

articles.title: NFL legend reveals why eating 'real food' after retirement led him to raise his own beef
articles.summary: Joe Thomas built Hall of Fame Farms from five cows and a bull into a 4,100-acre Wisconsin cattle operation focused on raising premium Wagyu beef.
articles.body: As the new NFL season kicks off Wednesday night, Pro Football Hall of Fame offensive lineman Joe Thomas is spending much of his time on a different kind of field. Thomas, the former Cleveland Browns offensive tackle famous for playing an NFL-record 10,363 consecutive snaps, has traded the trenches for tractors and cattle at Hall of Fame Farms, his roughly 4,100-acre operation in Wisconsin. For Thomas, farming was an ambition long before his playing days were over. CYCLOSPORA FEARS ARE SENDING SHOPPERS TO FARMERS MARKETS FOR LOCAL PRODUCE "I grew up outside of Milwaukee, did not grow up on a farm, but always just had a passion for being outside," Thomas said in a recent Fox News interview. "And then when I had the opportunity to go into the NFL, I said if there's only one thing I get out of the NFL, I want to be able to buy my own piece of dirt. I just want to have my own little farm." Thomas bought the original 1,200-acre property in 2012, while he was still playing for the Browns, and began with just five cows and a bull. Today, the operation encompasses about 4,100 acres, Thomas told Fox News, and raises hundreds of cattle, with an increasing focus on Wagyu beef. His interest in raising his own food intensified after his 2018 retirement. No longer needing to maintain the massive frame required of an NFL offensive lineman, Thomas said he lost weight and began paying closer attention to nutrition. "I wanted to try to focus on my health and be more intentional about eating real food," Thomas said. "And, so, I lost about 70 pounds when I retired, and I thought, 'Hey, what a great way to also know where my food came from.'" CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER His unusual second career has also attracted attention in Washington. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins recently visited Hall of Fame Farms and praised the former NFL star as an example of someone who entered agriculture without growing up in the industry. articles.summary: The NFL is back! The start of the 2026 regular season is now only hours away and will officially commence when the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots clash on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
The NFL is back! The start of the 2026 regular season is now only hours away and will officially commence when the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots clash on Wednesday evening.

For many fans, this means it's time to dive into season-long fantasy leagues, DFS games, prop bets, and survivor leagues.

Unfortunately, Week 1 can be extremely difficult for survivor players, as we simply don't know which teams are poised for a breakout or a regression. Sloppy play is often a hallmark of Week 1, too, which can lead to some very unexpected outcomes.

Let's not forget that the Las Vegas Raiders knocked off the New England Patriots in Week 1 last season.

Here, you'll find a few tips and tricks for navigating survivor play in 2026. You'll also find top picks for Week 1, using the latest odds as a guideline.

If you're a veteran of survivor leagues, you already know what to expect. For the uninitiated, here's a quick rundown.

Survivor pools typically require players to pick one team each week to win. If their selected squad loses, they're out. The caveat is that teams can generally only be picked once, which means simply picking the elite teams week in and week out isn't a viable strategy.

On the plus side, players only need to pick 18 teams to make it through the regular season, so flat-out bad franchises can be avoided more often than not. Of course, at this point in the season, we don't know who those teams truly are.

In Week 1, knowing which matchups to avoid entirely can be the key to survival. Players should generally stay away from divisional matchups, especially those in a prime-time window, as they often yield unexpected results.

The Los Angeles Rams, for example, are 3.5-point favorites over the rival San Francisco 49ers. While Los Angeles is a clear Super Bowl favorite and the better team on paper, it's hard to trust them against a familiar opponent on a Thursday night in Australia.

Waiting for the Rams' home opener against the New York Giants in Week 2 would be wise.

Similarly, the Denver Broncos should be able to handle the Kansas City Chiefs in Patrick Mahomes' first game back from a torn ACL. Winning in Aarrowhead on a Monday night will be tough, though, which is why Denver is actually a 2.5-point underdog.

Players should also be wary of games that involve multiple unknowns. The Tennessee Titans and New York Jets, for example, were both bad in 2025, but it's hard to know what to expect from either team in their Week 1 matchup. The Titans have a new head coach and several new players, while the Jets have a new quarterback and an upgraded offensive cast.

The Arizona Cardinals are bringing their fair share of variables to Week 1. They have a new head coach in Mike LaFleur and added a potential star running back in Jeremiyah Love —though Love has been dealing with an ankle sprain.

However, we should know what to expect from the Los Angeles Chargers, who will host Arizona in their opener.

Los Angeles has a terrific defense, which ranked fifth overall last season, and a potentially potent offense led by Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey, Omarion Hampton, and Quenton Johnston. With tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater again healthy, L.A.'s offense is poised to make a jump under new coordinator Mike McDaniel.

The Chargers are also likely to be very well prepared for Week 1, as Jim Harbaugh is one of the most buttoned-up coaches in the league. While other squads may be a bit shaky coming out of the preseason, the Chargers shouldn't be.

Los Angeles doesn't provide an overwhelming home-field advantage, but the Chargers are 9.5-point favorites for a reason. They're the better team by a considerable margin, and they should show that in Week 1.

Consider the Raiders Versus the Dolphins

Players looking to stick with "safe" picks in Week 1 should also consider the Detroit Lions (-6.5) against the New Orleans Saints or the Jacksonville Jaguars (-8.5) against the Cleveland Browns.

Those willing to gamble a bit right away should consider the Las Vegas Raiders (-3.5) against the Miami Dolphins.

Both teams are rebuilding in 2026, but it's easier to see the 2026 vision for Las Vegas than for Miami. The Raiders should be better right away, thanks to new pieces like head coach Klint Kubiak, quarterback Kirk Cousins, and center Tyler Linderbaum.

Las Vegas doesn't have a great roster overall, but it has some legitimate star power in players like Brock Bowers and Maxx Crosby. The Dolphins have a star running back in De'Von Achane, a potential star in quarterback Malik Willis, and not much else.

There's a reason why the Dolphins claimed a whopping seven players off waivers during cuts. Their roster is largely devoid of talent, and it's likely to struggle on the road in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Week 1 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fringe Fantasy Football Flex Starters
articles.summary: For many managers, Week 1 is the most difficult fantasy slate of the season that doesn't  involve bye weeks. We don't know which teams are good and which aren't just yet, and many player roles remain undefined.
articles.body:
For many managers, Week 1 is the most difficult fantasy slate of the season that doesn't involve bye weeks. We don't know which teams are good and which aren't just yet, and many player roles remain undefined.

Because of this, it's often best to stick with highly drafted stars who are known commodities. Players like Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Christian McCaffrey, and Puka Nacua may still disappoint in Week 1, but they're highly unlikely to flat-out bust.

Of course, managers can't simply depend on proven stars at every single position. Here, we'll examine some fringe starters who can be trusted or avoided based on past production, projected role, and individual matchups.

Start: MarShawn Lloyd, RB, Green Bay Packers

Green Bay Packers running back has been placed on the commissioner's exempt list to start the season, following a May arrest for misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage. This will likely leave Green Bay leaning heavily on MarShawn Lloyd to open the season.

Lloyd is expected to be the starter, though the Packers will likely use a committee that also includes Chris Brooks and trade acquisition Kaleb Johnson. In time, Johnson might even threaten Lloyd's status as RB1. However, that probably won't happen this week, as Johnson only arrived on August 30.

Expect Lloyd to get the bulk of the carries and a fair amount of receiving work this week against the rival Minnesota Vikings.

And while Minnesota's defense isn't exactly a favorable matchup, it did rank 21st in rushing yards allowed last season. It also surrendered more than 120 rushing yards in each of its two matchups against the Packers last season.

Sit: Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns

Cleveland Browns starting running back Quinshon Judkins should eventually return to form as a viable RB2 or flex starter. However, it's probably going to take some time, and managers should keep him on the sidelines in Week 1.

Judkins is coming off a dislocated ankle and fractured fibula that ended his rookie campaign. The Browns should be looking to ease him back into the lineup, which may mean a fair amount of pass-catching standout Dylan Sampson.

Even if Judkins is at 100 percent, he doesn't face an ideal matchup. The Jacksonville Jaguars surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs last season.

Add in the fact that we just don't know what to expect from Cleveland's offense under Todd Monken, and a wait-and-see approach with Judkins becomes very logical.

Start: Chris Godwin, WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Mike Evans departed in free agency, and most expect second-year wideout Emeka Egbuka to replace him as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' No. 1 receiver. However, veteran Chris Godwin is still around and should be a solid matchup-based option in 2026.

Injuries limited Godwin to only nine games last season, but he averaged a solid 3.7 catches and 40 yards per game.

The Cincinnati Bengals represent a good matchup for Godwin for a couple of reasons. Their defense is, on paper, significantly better than it was a year ago. However, it may take some time for things to tighten up, and Cincinnati ranked 29th in net yards per pass attempt allowed last season.

Secondly, the Bucs will likely need to lean on Baker Mayfield and the passing attack to keep pace with Cincinnati's explosive offense. That should mean targets for Godwin early and often.
