Sit: Marvin Harrison Jr., WR, Arizona Cardinals

In his two seasons with the Arizona Cardinals, Marvin Harrison Jr. has shown flashes of elite upside and playmaking ability. However, he's never played up to his status as the fourth overall pick.

Will new head coach Mike LaFleur unlock Harrison's potential in 2026? Perhaps, but it's hard to bet on the Ohio State product right out of the gate.

For one thing, Harrison was Arizona's third target behind Trey McBride and Michael Wilson by the end of last season. Secondly, the Cardinals are opening against a fantastic Los Angeles Chargers defense in L.A.

Los Angeles surrendered the 10th-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers last season.

articles.title: B/R's Week 1 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: The wait is over: The 2026 NFL season has arrived.
articles.body:
The wait is over: The 2026 NFL season has arrived.

The Seahawks host the Patriots on Wednesday night, launching both the new NFL season and another year of fantasy football.

After a summer of drafting fantasy rosters, it is time to focus on the Week 1 lineup. Put the players you selected in the best position to deliver an opening win and start the path toward the fantasy playoffs on the right foot.

Each week, Bleacher Report will provide tiered PPR rankings, a top-149 overall list and player analysis to help fantasy managers set their lineups.

The presence of two quarterbacks coming off injury-marred seasons in the top three underscores the uncertainty of Week 1 rankings.

We enter Week 1 with plenty of expectations, but fantasy football has a way of challenging them quickly. Stay flexible as the season begins to provide clearer answers.

Don't overthink your Week 1 lineup. If you drafted a clear starter under center, roll him out even if he's ranked a little lower here than you expected.

Also, don't be stunned if some big names start slow. Many of the high-end quarterbacks played sparingly or not at all in the preseason. It could take a little time to shake the rust off.

The cream of the crop occupies the first tier. Lamar Jackson draws a dream matchup against a Colts team that allowed more passing yards per game a year ago than any team in the AFC.

Josh Allen isn't so fortunate, travelling to Houston to face one of the NFL's best defenses. Joe Burrow faces a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks in 2025.

Most of the Tier 2 quarterbacks draw favorable matchups to open the season, highlighted by Jalen Hurts against a Washington Commanders defense that surrendered the second-most fantasy points per game to signal-callers a year ago.

Trevor Lawrence's home tilt against the Cleveland Browns isn't as good on paper. If you saw the Browns in the preseason, though, you will know that depth in their secondary is a major issue.

Fantasy managers aren't going to see Drake Maye ranked this low very often this year, but the last time we saw him against Seattle wasn't his best effort of last season.

Jayden Daniels is a major unknown early in the season, but so is an Eagles defense with issues on the edge.

Good luck figuring out what's going to happen with Stafford and the Rams in Australia. The strange circumstances of that game make him something of a crapshoot this week.

The fourth tier of quarterbacks this week are fringe starters with question marks.

What will Kyler Murray look like in his first start for the Minnesota Vikings. How healthy is Patrick Mahomes ahead of Monday's AFC West showdown with the Broncos? Can Baker Mayfield capitalize on a favorable Week 1 matchup with a Vikings defense that allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to QBs last season?

This tier consists primarily of matchup-dependent options.

Malik Willis has a favorable Week 1 matchup against the Raiders, although Miami's offensive outlook remains uncertain. Baltimore struggled against the pass last season, but Daniel Jones may have difficulty capitalizing given Indianapolis' unsettled receiving corps.

One or two quarterbacks in this tier could finish among the top 12 at the position, but they carry considerable risk.

Entering Week 1, these quarterbacks are low-confidence options even in superflex and two-quarterback formats and should not be considered in standard one-quarterback leagues.

The running back position could be especially difficult to evaluate in the early weeks of the season because several backfields and workloads remain unsettled.

Two higher-end backs—Ashton Jeanty of the Raiders and Jeremiyah Love of the Cardinals—enter the season nursing ankle injuries. Several backfields also remain unsettled, including those in Carolina, Green Bay, Minnesota, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay and Washington.

If you have clear lead backs, start them with confidence. Knowing a back is likely to receive 15-plus touches provides valuable lineup certainty, whether it is Week 1 or Week 11.

If you are considering a running back in an unsettled committee for a flex spot and have a similarly ranked wide receiver, the WR may be the safer Week 1 choice.

Fantasy managers paid a hefty price for these backs on draft day, and now it's time to start getting a return on that robust investment. Christian McCaffrey enters 2026 with understandable durability concerns, but he should continue to handle a substantial workload in Thursday's game in Australia.

Saquon Barkley could finish as the overall RB1 in Week 1 after the Commanders allowed the fifth-most PPR points per game to running backs last season.

The second tier of running backs are all solid Week 1 starts, just with a little less certainty and/or a slightly lower ceiling than the tier above them.

Omarion Hampton has a good chance to start hot against a Cardinals defense that led the NFC in PPR points per game given up to running backs a year ago. Javonte Williams faces a Giants team Sunday night that fielded the second-worst run defense in the league last year.

As we move into Tier 3, the questions start to add up, but these backs should all see solid workloads in Week 1 and a couple will likely end the week inside the top 12 at the position.

The Buffalo Bills fielded a bottom-five run defense, so David Montgomery's debut in Houston could be a big one.

Cam Skattebo has a favorable Week 1 matchup against a Dallas defense that may improve in 2026 but remains a potential vulnerability against the run.

Uncertainty increases in this tier, which includes few clear three-down backs.

The workloads for MarShawn Lloyd and Seahawks rookie Jadarian Price remain unsettled entering Week 1.

Quinshon Judkins projects as Cleveland's lead back, but he faces a Jacksonville defense that led the league by allowing only 85.6 rushing yards per game last season.

By Tier 5, committee backfields become a major concern.

Minnesota appears likely to deploy a true committee featuring Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones Sr.

Jonathon Brooks' Week 1 outlook became less secure when Chuba Hubbard returned to practice.

J.K. Dobbins projects as Denver's lead back, but the Broncos could manage his workload to preserve his availability.

Tier 6 options are best reserved for deep leagues or managers addressing lineup uncertainty.

Rachaad White could see increased receiving work if Washington plays from behind against Philadelphia, while Chris Rodriguez Jr. could limit Bhayshul Tuten's early-season workload.

These backs offer upside, but their roles and projections carry significant uncertainty.

These running backs are primarily players to monitor rather than recommended Week 1 starters.

George Holani and Chris Brooks could receive more work than expected, but most options in this tier need a clearer path to meaningful volume before becoming viable fantasy plays.

Wide receiver is a deeper and more stable position than running back. This isn't to say there aren't concerns, mostly due to injuries.

As a whole, though, the wideouts are less nerve-wracking than their counterparts in the backfield.

Once you get to WR4 territory, the waters start to muddy. But the odds are at least your top-three wideouts were drafted to be just that. So long as they are healthy, start the guys you drafted to start.

There will be ample time to panic soon enough.

This is the elite of the elite at wide receiver. These are players fantasy managers should start with a smile on their face on a weekly basis.

It's possible the game in Australia could get strange and affect Puka Nacua's stat line, but this quartet should feast on a weekly basis.

The second tier rounds out the fantasy WR1 for Week 1. It's a group that should have a relatively high floor as well as the potential for a smash week.

DeVonta Smith could deliver a big performance in his first game as Philadelphia's No. 1 receiver against a shaky Washington secondary.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens also have favorable upside in Dallas' Sunday night matchup against the Giants.

The Tier 3 wide receivers all have top-10 fantasy upside—it just comes with a little more uncertainty.

If Jaylen Waddle receives the target share I expect, this could be the lowest he is ranked all season.

At the other end of the spectrum, a healthy Rashee Rice has an elite ceiling. However, he draws a difficult Week 1 matchup against Patrick Surtain II and the Denver Broncos on Monday night.

There is considerable upside in this fourth tier, but each player also carries a notable question mark.

Jameson Williams has top-five potential, though his downfield role makes him a high-variance option. Parker Washington finished strongly for the Jaguars last season, but he is part of a crowded Jacksonville receiving corps.

Emeka Egbuka and Malik Nabers enter the season managing injuries, which adds uncertainty to their Week 1 outlooks.

Christian Watson has flashed in the past, but durability and week-to-week consistency remain concerns. Marvin Harrison Jr. could emerge as the focal point of Arizona's passing game, while Michael Wilson could continue to play a meaningful role with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback.

Cam Ward's development as a passer will also be a major factor in determining whether Carnell Tate can make an immediate fantasy impact as a rookie.

This tier includes several talented receivers, but each carries a lower floor or a more difficult Week 1 matchup.

Fantasy managers are hoping Brian Thomas Jr. rebounds in 2026, though he could face frequent coverage from Denzel Ward against Cleveland.

Stefon Diggs finished as a top-20 fantasy receiver in New England last season, but matching that production in Washington may be difficult.

De'Zhaun Stribling generated significant fantasy interest after an impressive preseason, but his role in San Francisco's offense remains uncertain.

Tre Tucker may enter Week 1 as Las Vegas' top wide receiver, though the value of that role will depend on how the Raiders' offense performs.

Tier 8 wide receivers are generally best reserved for deep leagues or emergency lineup situations in Week 1.

A player in this group could find the end zone and deliver a useful fantasy score, but the range of outcomes is wide and the floor is low.

Most managers should keep these receivers on the bench unless injuries, format requirements or unusually deep starting lineups leave few alternatives.

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

In recent years, the tight end position has done its level best to become as infuriating as the running backs. Stars such as Brock Bowers of the Raiders falter, while players like Harold Fannin Jr. of the Browns come from nowhere to have a big year.

Odds are that 2026 will bring more of the same uncertainty. With only Week 1 ahead, managers have limited information to work with, so there is no need to panic yet.

Unless you are streaming the position, start the tight end you drafted as your primary option. Week 1 uncertainty is normal, but most managers should avoid making a lineup change based solely on a marginal difference in the rankings.

Bowers and McBride begin the season in a tier of their own. A Tier 2 tight end could eventually join them, but for now they are a clear step above the rest of the position.

These tight ends are weekly starters with the potential to lead the position in scoring in any given week, along with floors that provide a measure of stability.

Colston Loveland enters 2026 with high expectations after a strong finish to the 2025 season.

With Tua Tagovailoa under center in Atlanta, Kyle Pitts could see a significant target share against a Steelers defense that allowed the second-most PPR points per game to tight ends last season.

Tier 3 tight ends carry a wide range of outcomes: They could finish among the position's top five in Week 1 or outside the top 15.

Fannin impressed as a rookie last season, but Cleveland's offensive changes create uncertainty around his 2026 outlook.

Tucker Kraft was productive before sustaining an ACL injury in 2025, and his snap count could be limited against Minnesota.

This tier is best approached as a group of matchup-dependent streamers. Kincaid offers the most upside, though his Week 1 matchup with Houston limits his projection.

Tier 5 tight ends are generally low-priority streaming options.

Greg Dulcich has some appeal as one of Miami's more experienced pass-catchers, but the Dolphins' offense showed limited consistency during the preseason.

This group offers occasional touchdown-dependent upside but carries low floors and significant week-to-week volatility.

Tier 6 is made up of low-end, matchup-dependent tight ends.

If George Kittle is unavailable for Thursday's game against the Rams in Australia, Jake Tonges could become a viable short-term replacement.

Otherwise, managers should look for stronger options unless they are in a particularly deep league or facing a roster emergency.

Fantasy managers generally took one of two approaches at defense on draft day: They drafted an every-week starter or planned to stream based on matchups. That strategy remains unchanged entering Week 1.

Managers who drafted elite defenses such as the Houston Texans or Denver Broncos may not love their opening matchups.

However, those matchups were known when drafts took place, and the benefit of investing in a high-end defense is the ability to start it confidently regardless of opponent, trusting that its playmaking can still produce a strong fantasy total.

Managers who stream defenses based on matchups may have more favorable options in Week 1. That approach requires regularly reassessing the schedule and using the waiver wire to identify the best available defense each week.

You had a plan on defense. Now execute it.

The Tier 1 defenses are atop the position this week because of matchups.

Cleveland and Arizona ranked among the 10 most favorable opponents for fantasy defenses in points allowed per game last season, while Atlanta also enters Week 1 with an uncertain offensive outlook.

Tier 2 consists largely of high-end defenses facing less-than-ideal Week 1 matchups.

The Rams, Texans and Broncos were the first three defenses selected on average during draft season.

There will be some volatility, but all three should produce more strong fantasy performances than disappointing ones in 2026.

Tier 3 includes capable defenses and matchup-dependent streaming options.

The Seattle Seahawks fit the first category in Wednesday night's matchup with the Patriots.

The Tennessee Titans are a matchup-driven play against a New York Jets offense that allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing defenses in 2025.

Tier 4 includes several volatile defenses with some matchup-driven upside.

The New York Jets are the most appealing option in this group, facing a Titans offense that allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to opposing defenses in 2025.

However, each defense in this tier carries a low floor and is best viewed as a high-risk streaming option.

The Raiders are a high-risk Week 1 streaming option.

Las Vegas is looking to improve after a poor defensive showing in 2025, and it opens against a Miami offense that allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to opposing defenses last season.

The matchup provides some upside, but the Raiders remain a volatile play until their defense shows meaningful progress.

There is little reason to overcomplicate the kicker position in Week 1. Start the kicker you drafted, ideally one attached to an efficient offense and a favorable matchup.

Reassess the position after the first two weeks, unless you have an elite option such as Brandon Aubrey or Cam Little.

This is a short list of kickers worth trusting early in the season. Little's exceptional range gives him one of the highest ceilings at the position.

Tier 2 blends established options such as Ka'imi Fairbairn with kickers like Evan McPherson and Jake Bates, who benefit from offenses expected to create frequent scoring opportunities.

This large tier offers a wide range of outcomes.

At least one kicker in this group could finish among the top five at the position in Week 1, but several could also fall outside the top 20.

Kicker scoring is highly volatile, making matchup and projected scoring environment especially important when choosing among these options.

Tier 4 kickers are best avoided outside of very deep leagues or emergency situations. Their projected scoring environments and individual outlooks make them low-confidence Week 1 options.

Before we get to the top 149 players overall (which can help with "flex" decisions) in Week 1, we have a couple of quick notes.

First, this list doesn't contain any quarterbacks. If you play in a "superflex" format and you can flex a quarterback, that's a good idea—unless that quarterback is Deshaun Watson.

Starting Watson is not a recommended option in fantasy this week.

Second, Week 1 brings plenty of excitement—and plenty of anxiety—for fantasy managers. No one wants to open the season 0-1, but that pressure can lead to overthinking and unnecessarily risky lineup decisions.

As we have said many times, relax. You drafted the players you did for a reason. Provided they are healthy in Week 1, there's no real reason to sit early-round picks outside the yips.

Don't start the season with your brain in pretzel-mode. It will get there soon enough regardless.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.summary: It's a new year for Bleacher Report's experts, and they're ready to lead you through another profitable season.
articles.body:
It's a new year for Bleacher Report's experts, and they're ready to lead you through another profitable season.

We're back with the same crew that includes analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford . Last season, Gagnon and Hanford led the group at 143-127-2 for the season. Moton finished third at 139-131-2.

Our panel will use the same format as last year, sharing all their picks and challenging each other with opposing views on every game unless there's a unanimous selection. We'll also keep track of lone-wolf picks, which were 32-29-1 last year.

Now, let's look ahead to the Week 1 slate, which starts Wednesday with the Super Bowl LX rematch and a lone-wolf pick right off the top.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 8, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks

I don't think the Super Bowl LX rematch will be as one-sided as last year's championship game. However, I do believe that Seattle's defensive front can prevent Drake Maye and the Patriots from finding an offensive rhythm once again.

With home-field advantage playing a factor, Seattle should win by more than a field goal and walk away with a 1-0 record.

It's understandable that the panel leaned heavily toward the Seahawks, given Seattle's dominant 29-13 victory over New England in Super Bowl LX six months ago. Since then, the Seahawks have lost key parts of that team and coaching staff.

Former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, who led Seattle's backfield with 1,027 yards and five touchdowns, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks also lost cornerback Riq Woolen and safety Coby Bryant in free agency.

Meanwhile, the Patriots added wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Running back TreVeyon Henderson won't play because of an ankle injury, though Rhamondre Stevenson has handled a workhorse role in the past. New England covers the 3.5-point spread.

Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams (in Australia)

There's no team entering the season with bigger hype than the Rams, and I'm buying it. While you could argue that the Rams' travel plans and a 49ers team that's probably more overlooked than they should be entering the season is a recipe for an upset, I think the Rams will show right away why they're the Super Bowl favorites. Rams win by a touchdown behind a dominant defensive performance.

Both teams have been major offseason headline generators: the Rams for building a super team headlined by the Myles Garrett trade and return of Aaron Donald; and the 49ers for what boils down to a lot of negativity headlined by injuries.

In fact, while almost all the focus has been on George Kittle's potential (likely?) return in Week 1, we don't actually know if Christian McCaffrey will be fit to play, and conventional wisdom would be to back the favorites. But these two teams traveled a long, long way to play a football game, and I'd rather take the points against a familiar foe in an unfamiliar setting regardless of who is on the field.

Rams: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski

Laying points on the road against arguably the NFL's best defense is starting the season with some anxiety. But I have that much more anxiety about C.J. Stroud after how he finished last season—Josh Allen leads the Bills to a close win on one of Week 1's better games.

Week 1 is a lot of gut, and I have a feeling the Houston defense will be extremely prepared for Buffalo in the Texans' home opener. That was certainly the case when they beat the Bills at this very site in November 2025. The Bills are an excellent team, but this is a tough spot for their new coach.

Texans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

The Bears enter this matchup with a shaky secondary. Safety Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and will miss a few months of action. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is on the physically unable to perform list with a calf injury.

However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young hasn't shown the ability to exploit opposing pass defenses' weaknesses, averaging just 180.2 passing yards per game over his three-year career.

Bears go on the road with their ascending offense and win by at least a field goal.

The Carolina Panthers finished among the bottom six in total offense last season. The organization added next-to-nothing to improve the unit. If anything, the group might be worse since both offensive tackle spots remain a serious concern. Conversely, the Chicago Bears are explosive enough offensively to easily cover this spread.

Bears: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars

I think the Browns could have some surprisingly nice moments this season, but this ain't the spot. Cleveland is, at the very least, a work in progress as a new core and coaching staff settle in. The Jaguars, on the other hand, are a well-oiled machine on a strong trajectory following a superb second half to the 2025 campaign. I expect them to keep rolling in their home opener.

Despite every expectation of the Cleveland Browns' offense imploding thanks to questionable quarterback setup, Todd Monken's squad gets the benefit of the doubt in the head coach's debut because of its defense. Myles Garrett might be gone, but this unit still has playmakers at all three levels to slow the Jaguars and make the contest interesting.

Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell

I don't trust the Steelers, and I hate that hook for them. It's really that simple. These teams are closer to being evenly matched than many might believe, and the Steelers were far from impressive at home in 2025. The Falcons didn't lose by more than a field goal in regulation in any of their last six road games last season. They should keep this game tight.

The jury is out on Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's reunion in Pittsburgh and the impact it will have on a stagnant Steelers offense, but I just don't see the "winner" of the NFL's least inspiring QB battle, Tua Tagovailoa, doing serious damage to the Steelers defense. I expect this game to be ugly, like most Steelers games are, but Tagovailoa makes one too many mistakes to give Pittsburgh as the clubs moves to 6-1 in its last 7 games ATS against Atlanta.

Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Fans who watch this entire game should receive some sort of reparations from the NFL. Neither offense in this slopfest can be trusted even a little, but for my money the Jets are slightly better defensively. First team to 13 points wins!

I'm inclined to believe it when I see it with Robert Saleh, Cam Ward, and the Titans. However, I believe they at least have the potential to turn things around quickly. The Jets? Not so much. I believe that New York is playing for 2027 and beyond.

I don't envision Tennessee running away with this one, but I don't see the Jets winning on the road, and this is awfully close to a pick 'em.

Titans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

The Saints closed last season red hot, and while some of that may be fool's gold, I think they'll keep this one within a touchdown. I expect Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Co. to have success against the Saints' defense, but I don't trust the Lions' secondary to give Tyler Shough major issues. Lions win by six in a high-scoring game.

Hey, the Saints are going to be feisty, and the panel is just about split on the Lions giving this many points for good reason. Missing the playoffs a year ago should be gnawing at Dan Campbell's group, though. Detroit scored an average of 32-plus points per game at home last season — a full touchdown more than on the road.

Can the Saints go toe-to-toe in a shootout with the Lions in Detroit? Maybe, but I'll back a first-week barrage from the stronger offensive unit as the Lions look to set the tone for a rebound campaign.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals

If Joe Burrow can stay healthy, Cincinnati's new-look defense should make the Bengals legitimate AFC contenders. However, the Bengals have been notorious for slow starts under Zac Taylor. I can't envision them winning big against a Buccaneers team that can play the underdog card after missing the playoffs in 2025.

Joe Burrow and Co. should hit the ground running. Can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers do the same without Mike Evans on the roster? Obviously, quarterback Baker Mayfield has other weapons in Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan. However, the Cincinnati Bengals still have an advantage in offensive firepower with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who were both back at practice this week

Bengals: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, Sobleski

Backing this many favorites at 3.5 makes me antsy, but I think the Ravens will be too much for the Colts here.

I'm not sold on the Ravens overall this season, but I think their improved defense under Jesse Minter, with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, should give them enough punch to make life very difficult for Daniel Jones. Lamar Jackson has to get back on track as a passer this season, but I think he makes enough plays to put Baltimore over the top.

Interestingly, the Indianapolis Colts' defense has a very specific matchup in its favor, with the defensive tackle duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart facing two brand-new starters along the Baltimore Ravens' offensive line. Thus, the Colts could control the line of scrimmage to make life difficult on quarterback Lamar Jackson and running back Derrick Henry. Offensively, Indianapolis should have all of its pieces back in place to get off to a hot start, as it did last season.

Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton

Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles

The Eagles have a lot of questions to answer on the offensive side of the ball in Week 1, but I'm just not buying the Commanders yet. Jayden Daniels is healthy, which will help, but the weapons around him leave some to be desired, and the absence of star LT Laremy Tunsil will loom large against an Eagles defense that loves to get after the quarterback.

I'm not sure Jalen Hurts silences the critics in Week 1, but I do think the Eagles have enough juice in the run game and on defense to control the game and win by a touchdown.

This is a divisional matchup, and both quarterbacks are learning new offenses. Expect both teams to be inefficient in a game of missed opportunities, while both defenses capitalize on miscues with takeaways.

Philadelphia also lost some offensive explosiveness when it traded three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. On the ground, running back Saquon Barkley helps the Eagles grind out a close victory by a margin short of a touchdown.

Commanders: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Neither of these teams are especially easy to trust in the early-going this year—the Vikings have a new quarterback in Kyler Murray and the Packers have significant questions on defense, especially where the pass rush is concerned. I'll take the points—with exactly zero confidence.

I don't know how I feel about the Packers opening the season on the road against a sneaky-good division rival without Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons. Throw in the unpredictability factor with Kyler Murray, and I think Green Bay is in a tough situation here.

Packers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

This will be one of the rare moments in the season that laying more than a field goal on the Raiders is a reasonable position on their spread.

Both teams are in rebuild mode, but Las Vegas has star power in its favor. After missing five games with a PCL injury last season, All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers is healthy. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is optimistic about running back Ashton Jeanty suiting up after he suffered an ankle injury during practice on August 23.

Although the Raiders have an unproven secondary with rookie second-rounder Treydan Stukes likely to play at safety and second-year pro Darien Porter at the No. 2 cornerback spot, quarterback Kirk Cousins is more equipped to dice up a shaky pass defense than Malik Willis. Bowers and Jeanty lead Las Vegas to a win by a touchdown.

Woof. Two organizations in complete rebuild mode. Two new starting quarterbacks under new coaching staffs. Just give me the points in this one, and I'll figure out what to do with these two for the rest of the season after Week 1.

Raiders: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers

To be clear, the Arizona Cardinals have about as much chance of winning this game as I do of winning an Academy Award. But Arizona has talent on offense and showed it can move the ball last season—Jacoby Brissett will lead a garbage-time touchdown drive late and the Redbirds will sneak in the back door for the cover.

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been teammates with his top pass-catchers for multiple years, and the team added tight end David Njoku, who has 384 receptions for 4,062 yards and 34 touchdowns in his nine-year career.

With newly established offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel calling the plays, the Chargers could score in flurries against the Cardinals, who retained defensive coordinator Nick Rallis after his unit gave up the fourth-most points last season.

Chargers: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Will the Giants be better under new head coach John Harbaugh? Yes. Are they prepared to keep pace with a team that has one of the NFL's top offenses and a vastly improved defense? At this point in the season, I don't believe so.

Week 1 divisional matchups can be unpredictable, and I won't be shocked if the Giants steal this one. I think it's far more likely that Dallas makes one or two defensive plays that it wouldn't have made a year ago to preserve a one-score victory.

The Cowboys are the better team on paper, and the Giants' secondary will have a hard time defending CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens even if Big Blue is getting to Dak Prescott.

But if a new coaching staff and the return of two injured star players to the lineup (Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers), on top of two rookie first-round picks starting in their debuts (Arvell Reese and Francis Mauigoa), at home on Sunday Night Football against a bitter rival, isn't enough to get a team up, then what in the gorydamn hell are we playing this game for?

Cowboys: Davenport, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Winning as the road team in Kansas City is tough, but defense travels, and the Broncos have one of the best in the business. Beyond that, I think it's going to take a few games for Patrick Mahomes to find his groove with whatever post-injury playing style he brings to the 2026 season.

The Chiefs will go as Mahomes does, and one or two instances of him hesitating behind the line will sink them against arguably the most well-rounded team in the conference.

The Denver defense is going to be a problem for Kansas City, especially with a less than 100% healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. On paper, the Broncos might be the better all-around team, too.

And, the Chiefs have lost two of the last three season openers, with the lone victory being a controversial end-of-game call that gave K.C. the victory over Baltimore in 2024. Yeah, all things point to a Broncos cover, if not an outright win. So, I'll ride with the minority and lay these points with the home team covering late.

Broncos: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

articles.title: The NFL season officially kicks off tonight. Here are 5 things to watch in the first week of games
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are loaded, Patrick Mahomes has a new knee, the Super Bowl champs are somehow underdogs and Buffalo Bills fans are once again convincing themselves this is the year!
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams are loaded, Patrick Mahomes has a new knee, the Super Bowl champs are somehow underdogs and Buffalo Bills fans are once again convincing themselves this is the year! It’s all happening in the NFL. Here are five things to know about Week 1 of the 2026 season. The Rams are big, big favorites The Los Angeles Rams enter the season as huge favorites to win the Super Bowl, which will be played in LA for the first time since… the Rams won the Super Bowl in 2022. It’s been a blockbuster offseason for the Rams. They made a huge trade, sending three draft picks, including a first-rounder, to the Browns for superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett. They also made a big trade with the Chiefs, sending four draft picks, including a first-rounder, for star cornerback Trent McDuffie. Those moves instantly made the Rams one of the scariest defenses in the league. And that was BEFORE arguably the best defensive player of all time decided to come out of retirement. For the first time since the 2023 season, Aaron Donald will suit up for the Rams. The 35-year-old, three-time Defensive Player of the Year, now teams up with Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Good luck to the offensive lines facing the Rams this season. Sean McVay’s team is the overwhelming favorite to win the Super Bowl at +500. That may not be great news for the Rams, though, because teams that have been so heavily favored are 0-20 over the last 30 years. The big question for this team, other than whether it can stay healthy: Can Matthew Stafford repeat last year’s MVP performance at 38 years old? The 49ers’ wild off-season The Rams will open the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia on Thursday on Netflix. It certainly has been an interesting offseason for the Niners. Head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a serious car accident in July that left him with a severe concussion, a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand and a large gash near his right eye that required more than 40 stitches. Then owner Jed York was arrested in an undercover prostitution sting in Ohio. York was charged with misdemeanor counts of engaging in prostitution and possession of criminal tools, referring to his cellphone. The prostitution charge was amended to misdemeanor disorderly conduct, and York pleaded no contest to both disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools. He received a two-day jail sentence, with credit for time served, and was ordered to pay $1,150 in fines. Then came the Daeshon Love saga. Love was arrested by the FBI on August 24 for allegedly executing an elaborate, multiyear romance scam in which he posed as a 49ers wide receiver. Love has nothing to do with the actual 49ers, but the story just added to one of the most bizarre offseasons for a team in a long time. On the field, the 49ers still have Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey and added star receiver Mike Evans. They are expected to be good once again, but they play in the toughest division in football, the NFC West. (And yes, they still practice next to the electrical substation.) The Seahawks think no one believes in them It’s pretty rare for the reigning Super Bowl champion to not even be the favorite to win its division the following year. The Seahawks dominated the playoffs last season and destroyed the New England Patriots in the Super Bowl, but somehow they still have that “no one believes in us” attitude. The reigning champs return nearly everyone from last year’s team, minus Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, who signed with the Chiefs in the offseason. Right now, Seattle has the third-best odds to win it all, behind the Rams and Bills. Much is made of the Seahawks’ “12th Man,” the name for their fans, who give the team a great home-field advantage in Seattle. But head coach Mike Macdonald has proven he knows how to get his squad ready on the road, too. Through two seasons, Macdonald is 15-2 on the road, the second-best record all time for a coach in his first two seasons, behind only George Seifert. The Seahawks will open the season Wednesday at home in a Super Bowl rematch against the Patriots. Mahomes’ return from ACL injury Last season marked the end of the Chiefs’ dynasty run. Mahomes, Andy Reid and company had gone to seven straight AFC championship games, five Super Bowls and won three of them during an incredible run from 2018-24. But last year was a struggle. Mahomes and the offense never looked right … and then, in December, Mahomes tore his ACL, effectively ending the Chiefs’ season and halting the team’s run of 10 straight years in the playoffs. Now the question is: Can Mahomes and the Chiefs recapture that magic? Mahomes is on target to start the season despite being just nine months removed from the ACL tear. Travis Kelce is back, fresh off marrying Taylor Swift in the offseason. And, as mentioned, the Chiefs added Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, giving them their best threat out of the backfield since they had a young Kareem Hunt back there. The Chiefs also get to play a third-place schedule, which should help this season. But the AFC West is expected to be very tough, with the Broncos and Chargers also hoping to contend for a conference title. The Chiefs open the season at home on Monday Night Football against the Broncos. Is it finally Josh Allen’s year? Every year for a while now, the Bills have been one of the preseason favorites. And every year their season somehow ends in disappointment. Josh Allen is the best quarterback in football. He pretty much guarantees you have a chance. But Bills fans are hoping that FINALLY the ball will bounce their way and they will find themselves in the Super Bowl. Their last Super Bowl appearance was in 1994, when they lost their fourth straight championship game. This is Year Nine for Allen. His worst record since his rookie season is 10-6. You can pretty much book it: The Bills are going to somehow win 10 to 13 games in the regular season. But that’s getting old in Buffalo. The fan base is yearning for a Super Bowl run. This season, they have a brand-new stadium – with some questionable obstructed-view seats – to enjoy. Allen is arguably the best quarterback ever to not play in a Super Bowl. So it’s going to happen at some point… right? This season will be a battle. The Bills have a tough schedule, and it starts in Houston against the Texans’ stellar defense in Week 1.

articles.title: Which NFL team should you support? Trophies, temperature and history - take our quiz
articles.summary: As the NFL returns for a new season, BBC Sport helps you choose your ideal team to follow.
articles.body:
Some 213 days after the Seattle Seahawks beat the New England Patriots at Super Bowl 60, the NFL returns, with the same sides meeting again to open the season.

On Wednesday (01:20 BST, Thursday) the Patriots travel to Lumen Field to play a Seahawks team hoping to become only the ninth franchise to win the title in consecutive seasons.

If you're in the market for a team to follow this year, BBC Sport is here to help.

We've crunched the numbers on a wide range of categories to put the information at your fingertips - and there's a handy quiz at the end to help you figure out your best fit.

Let's start with the top dogs - the trophy winners.

Leading the way with six Super Bowls each are the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Patriots, the latter all coming since the turn of the century under legendary coach Bill Belichick.

Not far behind are the Dallas Cowboys, known as 'America's team', and the San Francisco 49ers, who have each won five.

Taking in the pre-Super Bowl era, the Green Bay Packers have the most NFL championships with 13, including four Super Bowl wins.

At the other end of the spectrum, 12 franchises have never won the Vince Lombardi Trophy, including the Buffalo Bills and the Minnesota Vikings, who have both lost four times in the Super Bowl.

Perhaps silverware isn't everything to you.

If history is more your bag, four teams have been around for 100 years or more. The Arizona Cardinals, Chicago Bears, New York Giants and Green Bay Packers were all established in the 1920s.

For those who prefer more modern upstarts, look no further than the Houston Texans, who only started competing in the NFL in 2002.

We took a calculation of the centre of the UK being a location in Lancashire and figured out the distance from that point to each franchise's stadium in the US.

East Coast teams such as the New England Patriots, Philadelphia Eagles and the two New York teams - the Giants and Jets - are the closest by that metric, coming in at just over 3,000 miles away.

If you would prefer to get as far away from home as possible, shoot across the US towards the Pacific Ocean and opt for the Los Angeles Chargers or Rams, fully 5,263 miles away as the crow flies.

Any NFL game is a major event and, as amply demonstrated during the football World Cup this summer, the US is full of stadiums to suit.

We took the average attendance for each team over the past five seasons to calculate the biggest - and it was the AT&T Stadium in Dallas, where England played their opening group game against Croatia.

The lowest average was the Chicago Bears, with element-exposed Soldier Field the only stadium to come in under 60,000.

The franchise are developing plans for a venue across the state border in Hammond, Indiana.

Who has the warmest and coolest climate?

Taking US weather data from 1991 to 2020, we looked at the range of temperatures from highest to lowest across all 32 areas.

It is no surprise that the hottest areas will affect desert teams Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, with Florida's Miami Dolphins and Tampa Bay Buccaneers also offering scorching summers and mild winters.

If that is not for you, then 12 franchises have an average lowest temperature under freezing, including the Vikings, whose average in January is -8C.

Since first jetting to London in 2013, the Jacksonville Jaguars have played in the UK 14 times, and will stretch that further when they play back-to-back weeks there in October.

That number far outstrips every other franchise, with the Buffalo Bills playing six times in the now defunct Toronto Series of the mid-2000s and twice in London, and the Miami Dolphins third with seven overseas games.

The NFL continues to extend its reach with nine international games planned for 2026, including a maiden trip to Australia when the San Francisco 49ers face the LA Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on opening weekend.

The Dallas Cowboys, whose only previous appearance on foreign soil was in 2014 at Wembley against the Jaguars, will play the Baltimore Ravens at another iconic world stadium, the Maracana in Rio de Janeiro, at the end of September.

articles.title: "Chiefs and chiefskingdom is with you!": How a quiet Patrick Mahomes DM to a grieving Chiefs analyst became the most emotional story of the NFL season
articles.summary: NFL News: Tucker Franklin does not play for the Kansas City Chiefs. He does not suit up. He is a content manager and podcast co-host at KC Sports Network, a You.
articles.body: Tucker Franklin does not play for the Kansas City Chiefs. He does not suit up. He is a content manager and podcast co-host at KC Sports Network, a YouTube channel with 33,400 subscribers built around deep-dive Chiefs breakdowns. But last week, when his father Doug passed away unexpectedly on August 31, the quarterback of the Kansas City Chiefs slid into his DMs. Patrick Mahomes, days away from his Week 1 comeback after tearing his ACL, took time to type out a message to a grieving media member he had never shared a locker room with.What did Patrick Mahomes say to Tucker Franklin after his father's death?Franklin broke the news of his father's passing on X, and the response from the sports media community was immediate. Nearly 600 replies poured in. But it was one message in particular, buried inside Franklin's private inbox, that stopped everything.Mahomes had sent him a direct message.Franklin posted a screenshot of it on Sunday night. Simple. Unannounced. No press team involved. Just a quarterback checking on someone hurting."Praying for your family, man," Mahomes wrote. "Chiefs and ChiefsKingdom is with you!"Franklin replied the way most people would when something hits them right in the chest."Man, thank you so much for reaching out. Means more than you'll know. I appreciate you," he wrote back.Mahomes read it. He reacted with a heart emoji. That was it.But Franklin did not keep it to himself. He shared the screenshot publicly, and the framing around it said everything about what it meant to him."I think it's easy to wonder if the quarterback of your favorite team is actually a good guy," Franklin wrote. "We don't have to wonder about that in KC."The post caught fire. NFL writers, podcasters, fellow media personalities all reacted. Matt Verderame, who co-hosts That Football Show alongside Franklin on KCSN, called it a class act. Others echoed the same. It was the kind of thing that does not need a lot of words to land.Why does this Mahomes moment matter beyond the feel-good story?There is a version of this story that is just a nice thing an athlete did. And it is that. But it is also something a little more specific to the NFL right now.Mahomes is in the middle of a miraculous comeback from a torn ACL. He is preparing to face the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football in Week 1. His plate is full. The scrutiny on his recovery alone has been relentless. And yet, somewhere between film sessions and rehab and the noise of a season opener against an AFC West rival, he tracked down a media member's inbox and sent him three sentences.Franklin has spent years building video essays and breakdowns about a franchise he clearly loves. His Twitter bio reportedly calls him a "Patrick Mahomes Propagandist," which is a funny way of saying he genuinely believes in the guy. That belief just got confirmed in the most personal way possible.What makes this land differently than the standard athlete-does-good-thing story is the absence of any performance in it. No cameras. No coordinated social post. Franklin made it public. Mahomes did not. That detail is not small.Chiefs Kingdom, as it gets called, is a real thing in Kansas City. It is the community around the team, the fans, the media, the people who care. Mahomes pointed at that in his message. He was not just speaking for himself. He was speaking for all of it. And right now, a week before the season starts, that is the kind of thing that cuts through every noise around him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Legendary sports agent gives Fernando Mendoza simple advice after Raiders benching to begin career
articles.summary: Legendary sports agent Leigh Steinberg said Fernando Mendoza should study how Patrick Mahomes and Aaron Rodgers thrived after sitting behind veteran quarterbacks early on.
articles.body: Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will begin his career on the bench, no easy thing for a No. 1 overall pick who just won a national championship. Legendary agent Leigh Steinberg, who had eight No. 1 overall draft picks as clients in his illustrious career, said he would tell Mendoza to look at the success of other star quarterbacks who sat on the bench to begin their careers. "All competitive athletes want to play, but I would point out to Mendoza that Patrick Mahomes sat for a whole year behind Alex Smith in Kansas City. And when he came out his second year, he was MVP," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview. "Aaron Rodgers had a similar route. That Philip Rivers had a similar route." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Mahomes played just one game his rookie season, the final game of the regular season, before taking over as the full-time starter in 2018 and winning the MVP.
