articles.title: 'Scared S--tless,' Caleb Williams' Heroics During Bears' Playoff Run Had NFL Team Dreading Matchup
articles.summary: While he's generally not considered to be elite at his position just yet, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams isn't somebody teams are eager to see in a playoff setting.
articles.body:
While he's generally not considered to be elite at his position just yet, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams isn't somebody teams are eager to see in a playoff setting.

The Athletic's Jeff Howe said one contender was "scared s--tless" at the idea of matching up against Chicago with its season on the line. That was down entirely to Williams' penchant for stepping up when the lights are their brightest.

The Bears signal-caller helped engineer six fourth-quarter comebacks during the regular season, the most in the league.

The team's NFC Wild Card Round win over the Green Bay Packers epitomized what sets Williams apart. He threw two interceptions and only completed 50 percent of his passes, but he also was the spark behind Chicago scoring 25 points in the fourth quarter.

You can count on one hand the number of NFL quarterbacks capable of pulling off Williams' fourth-down completion to Rome Odunze. Flushed out of the pocket, he threw against his body on the move and threaded the ball perfectly to his wideout.

Howe wrote that "there's also a consistent opinion around the NFL that Williams must be more consistent on schedule to really elevate his game." It's a fair assessment when Williams completed fewer than 60 percent of his attempts and ranked 16th in QBR (58.2).

But the 2025 season provided a proof of concept for why the 2022 Heisman Trophy winner was so hyped coming out of college and why the Bears identified him as their franchise quarterback.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 1
articles.summary: The 2026 regular season is here, football fans. The Seattle Seahawks will begin their title defense on Wednesday night with a Super Bowl LX rematch against the New England Patriots. That game will mark the start of an 18-week marathon to the NFL playoffs.
articles.body:
The 2026 regular season is here, football fans. The Seattle Seahawks will begin their title defense on Wednesday night with a Super Bowl LX rematch against the New England Patriots. That game will mark the start of an 18-week marathon to the NFL playoffs.

While the focus has pivoted from roster construction to on-field action, fans can expect to see more trades between now and the November 10 deadline. Some teams are entering Week 1 with notable needs, while others will experience attrition during the long campaign.

Still other teams will look to cash in assets for draft capital as they begin falling out of contention.

We are unlikely to see a flurry of trade activity early in the season, but it's never too soon to examine the top candidates. Here, you'll find our top 10 trade targets, ranked based on past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, likely availability, and any relevant buzz.

We'll also project trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, while providing some logical suitors for each player on our list.

10. Brandon Aiyuk, WR, San Francisco 49ers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 7th-Round Pick

If a team becomes desperate for wide receiver help, it can probably have San Francisco 49ers pass-catcher Brandon Aiyuk for next to nothing. The 49ers have made it clear that they're ready to move on from their former standout, and they've practically begged teams to take him off their hands all offseason.

"We're available. Give us a call," general manager John Lynch told reporters in his post-draft press conference.

The question is whether a team will become desperate enough to make a move for Aiyuk after repeatedly attacking his current team on social media. The Washington Commanders were reportedly interested in signing him if he had become available, but have lost some interest, according to ESPN's Nick Wagoner and John Keim :

"The phrase you'll hear is 'never say never,' but there's been a definite cooling of the Commanders' interest after Aiyuk's Instagram postings over the past month, including some about [Washington QB Jayden] Daniels."

On the positive side, Aiyuk is still only 28 years old and surpassed 1,300 receiving yards when last healthy in 2023.

Potential Suitors: Houston Texans, Miami Dolphins

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick

While J.J. McCarthy's time with the Minnesota Vikings isn't officially over just yet, it certainly feels like the clock is ticking. Minnesota named Kyler Murray as its Week 1 starter and has veteran Carson Wentz set to provide backup duties.

McCarthy could still salvage his career with the Vikings, but it might require a special set of circumstances for the 2024 first-round pick to even get that opportunity. Minnesota, meanwhile, may be willing to part with McCarthy sooner rather than later, provided it can get an acceptable return.

According to veteran NFL reporter Jason La Canfora, the Vikings will hope to attack value to McCarthy's future playing time.

"As part of any finalised deal, the Vikings are also expected to seek a conditional element in any deal that would increase their compensation, should McCarthy go on to play for his new team," La Canfora wrote for Casino.org.

Right now, McCarthy would be most attractive to teams looking to develop a long-term backup or simply take a flier on a former first-round pick.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Los Angeles Chargers

8. Xavier Legette, WR, Carolina Panthers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

Teams looking to take a flier on a former first-round pick are exactly the sort that could be interested in Carolina Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette. Aside from his draft status and physical upside, the third-year receiver has shown little else to offer.

Through two seasons with the Panthers, the 32nd overall pick out of South Carolina has tallied just 84 catches for 860 yards and seven touchdowns. He also battled foot and ankle injuries that caused him to miss time during the preseason.

With at least two years left on his rookie contract, the Panthers would probably prefer to see Legette live up to his draft status in Carolina. After seeing him record just 363 yards as the team's No. 2 target behind Tetairoa McMillian in 2025, though, they may also have him on a short leash.

If Jalen Coker can stay healthy and free-agent addition John Metchie III can force himself into a prominent role, the Panthers could quickly decide to cash in Legette for draft capital. Teams looking to add a 6'1", 221-pound pass-catcher with 4.39 speed should be willing to take a chance on him.

Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, Las Vegas Raiders

Will a non-QB be 2027's No. 1 pick? New NFL mock draft

Late Additions Who Could Influence Super Bowl Hopes 💪

7. Joey Porter Jr., CB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 1st-Round Pick

The Pittsburgh Steelers seem to believe they can make another run at the playoffs with Aaron Rodgers and new head coach Mike McCarthy. Unless their perception changes, they probably won't be eager to move starting cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , however, the Steelers aren't overly eager to extend Porter early either, which could force the team to make him available:

" Sources say the Steelers' lack of a formal offer for weeks sent the clear message to Porter that they would like him to play out the final year of his rookie contract, which prompted him to consider the possibility of a trade or sitting out for an extended period."

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport recently told The Pat McAfee Show that he still believes an extension could get done before the start of the season. Porter would rank higher on this list if it was more clear that he could be acquired.

However, trading for the 26-year-old would be costly, both in terms of compensation and the ensuing contract that would be required to keep him. His market could be limited to playoff hopefuls with cap space to spare.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Cleveland Browns made one for-the-future move when they dealt Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. They could make another—albeit with a much smaller return—by trading away wide receiver Jerry Jeudy.

The Browns used early draft picks on wide receivers K.C. Concepcion and Denzel Boston , which could push Jeudy out of the long-term plan. Tony Grossi of The Land on Demand believes the two rookies could push Jeudy out in the not-too-distant future.

"Now, from what I've seen of Boston and Concepcion, Jeudy could be a real trade chip played by GM Andrew Berry at the November 10 deadline, if not earlier," Grossi said in August (h/t Max Dible of Heavy).

Jeudy had a down year in 2025, along with the rest of the Browns' offense. However, he was a Pro Bowler in 2024 and is still only 27 years old. He should interest receiver-needy teams, and his $1.5 million base salary for 2026 is extremely team-friendly.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs

Projected Trade Value: 2027 1st-Round Pick, 2028 1st-Round Pick

Las Vegas Raiders pass-rusher Maxx Crosby would be at the top of our list if the Raiders were actively shopping him. After their offseason agreement with the Baltimore Ravens fell through, though, Las Vegas seems perfectly content to keep Crosby as the face of its defense.

Baltimore, you may remember, voided the trade after Crosby's physical raised health and durability concerns.

For now, Crosby is a Raider again, but that doesn't mean he's off limits. According to ESPN's Ryan McFadden , Las Vegas wasn't actively looking to move Crosby in the spring before Baltimore made an offer it couldn't refuse.

"For the Raiders to part ways with their franchise cornerstone, they needed an offer that included multiple first-round picks, similar to the trade of Micah Parsons from Dallas to Green Bay last August," McFadden wrote.

If another team comes calling about Crosby, the Raiders will undoubtedly listen. They're in the early stages of a rebuild and may not be ready to contend while Crosby is still in his playing prime.

The asking price will be high, but teams that believe they can chase a Super Bowl are bound to target him before November 10.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, New England Patriots

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick and/or Veteran Player

Though they probably won't go after a player like Crosby, the Cincinnati Bengals very well could be sneaky Super Bowl contenders in 2025. They tend to be relevant when Joe Burrow is able to stay healthy, and they actually took an aggressive approach to addressing their defense this season.

As part of Cincinnati's defensive overhaul, it added interior linemen Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. Their additions could potentially lead the Bengals to make fellow defensive tackle T.J. Slaton available for the right price.

Slaton is in the final year of his contract and is set to carry a $9.2 million cap hit in 2026.

For Cincinnati, Slaton can provide value in a DT rotation that includes Lawrence, Allen, B.J. Hill, Kris Jenkins Jr., and Landon Robinson . If he only sees sporadic playing time, though, he could be even more valuable as a trade chip.

With the Bengals looking to win now, they would probably want a player who can help them rather than a future draft pick, though that could change if guys like Jenkins and Robinson prove capable enough. And Slaton should have a strong trade market, as good defensive tackles are almost always in demand.

Potential Suitors: Green Bay Packers, Indianapolis Colts

Arizona Cardinals edge-rusher Josh Sweat was the topic of trade speculation early in the offseason. Though Sweat didn't publicly ask for a trade, Cardinals insider Kyle Odegard reported in May that he had "been hearing for awhile" that he "is not particularly happy" in Arizona.

For now, though, Arizona appears uninterested in making Sweat available.

"The Cardinals are telling interested teams they aren't planning to trade Sweat, and I believe that to be true," ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote.

Of course, the Cardinals' stance is likely to change when and if it begins falling out of the NFC West race.

As much as Arizona may believe it can win with Jacoby Brissett and may like rookie quarterback Carson Beck , the reality is that its QB of the future may not be on the current roster. Moving Sweat could net valuable capital with which to build around said quarterback.

While Sweat will turn 30 in the offseason, he's coming off a 12-sack campaign and should easily command a conditional pick that can become a Day-2 selection with relatively minimal incentives.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 2nd-Round Pick

With Baker Mayfield agreeing to a three-year extension with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Tuesday, Brock Purdy might be trending as the top quarterback on the 2027 free-agent market. With the position pool likely to be headlined by QBs like Jacoby Brissett, Deshaun Watson, and Geno Smith, Jones might be the only quarterback teams are willing to target as a potential long-term starter.

While the Alabama product significantly regressed after his Pro Bowl rookie campaign with the New England Patriots, he revitalized his stock as a spot starter with the San Francisco 49ers last season.

Jones went 5-3 as a starter while throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions last season.

Teams that do view Jones as a potential QB1 could look to make a preemptive trade to acquire him now—which would open up the possibility to use the franchise tag for an audition in 2027.

Jones is obviously a valuable backup behind Brock Purdy, but the 49ers should be willing to trade him for a price. The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported that San Francisco was looking for a second-round pick and more early in the offseason.

The market for Jones will peak if and when another contender loses its starting quarterback to injury. However, QB-needy teams who are looking ahead could come calling, too.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns

1. Kayvon Thibodeaux, Edge, New York Giants

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 3rd-Round Pick

Good pass-rushers will always have a trade market. While Kayvon Thibodeaux had just 2.5 sacks last season, he's shown flashes of being a very good sack artist. In 2023, he recorded 11.5 sacks and 35 quarterback pressures.

The issue for Thibodeaux is that the New York Giants' top edge-rusher is Brian Burns, and they added Abdul Carter near the top of the 2025 draft. In April, New York added Arvell Reese , who will begin his career as an off-ball linebacker but who has the potential to move to the edge early in his career.

Given his lack of production over the past couple of seasons, it's hard to envision Thibodeaux having a lengthy future in New York—and the Giants have at least had discussions about moving him.

According to Dan Duggan of The Athletic, the Giants were in talks with the New Orleans Saints during draft weekend, though their asking price of a second-round pick was not amenable to New Orleans.

If Thibodeaux doesn't earn a prominent role early under new head coach John Harbaugh, the Giants should listen to offers once again. This time around, a third-rounder that can become a second-round pick with incentives may be enough to put him on a pass-rush-needy defense.

Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: 5 Cleveland Browns Under the Most Pressure Entering the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The NFL is a high-pressure environment. From expiring contracts to fifth-year options to constant coaching turnover, the most important thing for every player is what they've done lately.
articles.body:
The NFL is a high-pressure environment. From expiring contracts to fifth-year options to constant coaching turnover, the most important thing for every player is what they've done lately.

Throw a struggling team like the Cleveland Browns into that kind of pressure cooker and the intensity is kicked up a notch.

The 2026 version will be focused on evaluation as Todd Monken and his staff take over the team. While everyone is going to have to prove themselves moving forward, some are under a bigger microscope than others.

Here are the five Browns under the most pressure entering Week 1.

Some pressure fell off Shedeur Sanders shoulders when the team named Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback. Yet, it still feels like a do-or-die season for the second-year passer.

Watson being named the starter gives Sanders some time to continue his development as the backup. At the same time, it takes away opportunities for him to show that he can be the solution at quarterback in 2027.

If Watson starts all 17 games it's going to be hard to justify passing up on a quarterback prospect in the 2027 class to roll with Sanders in his third season.

Sanders will need to find his way on the field and do more than he did in his rookie season if he wants to be the starter in 2027. Facing that kind of pressure when he isn't even the starter at the beginning of the year is putting plenty on his plate.

The Browns went full remodel on their offensive line this offseason. They drafted Spencer Fano in the first round to anchor the left side, but they mostly did the rest with short-term free agent deals.

Teven Jenkins is the only projected starting lineman who started for the Browns last season. The team brought Jenkins back on a one-year, $4 million contract this offseason.

He'll start the season as the right guard after starting four of the final five games of the year in 2025. It might be his final chance to prove he can be a long-term solution on the interior of the line.

The Browns used a third-round pick on Austin Barber. The Florida product has experience at tackle, but is listed as the backup guard. Jenkins might have to play at a level that convinces Cleveland to hand him a mutli-year contract if he wants to be on the roster in 2027.

Myles Garrett is out, and Jared Verse is in, but it's Isaiah McGuire who could be feeling the pressure this season.

Verse is a good, young piece to build around. He also knows there are future first-round picks coming to help fill out the Garrett trade. McGuire is being thrust into a role where he has to be more than a rotational depth piece.

McGuire played 41 percent of the snaps last season and registered 29 pressures . Those aren't bad numbers, but there are a lot of one-on-one blocking situations when you have Garrett on one side of the defensive line.

Alex Wright was supposed to be the edge-rusher across from Verse leading the pass rush. He was third on the team with 5.5 sacks. Unfortunately, his ruptured Achilles has thrust McGuire into the spotlight.

McGuire is in he final year of his rookie contract. He's set up to score a major payday if he can become the secondary pass-rusher on the defense. He'll need to take a big leap up from 2.5 sacks last season to make that happen.

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Andrew Berry made his thoughts on the Browns receiving weapons pretty clear on draft day.

The offense needed firepower and they spent premium picks on KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston to get it. It's clear the front office is looking to go young to build an enticing core for a quarterback that may or may not be on the roster.

Right now, he appears to be on the way out. He has combined for 23 drops in his two seasons with Cleveland. Browns quarterbacks had a passer rating of 43.8 when targeting him last season.

Jeudy's contract made it hard to move on from him this offseason. Next year, he could be released with a post-June 1 cut to generate some savings.

The pressure is on for Jeudy to prove that he can be an asset to the pass game as the Browns try to find an identity under Todd Monken.

This is the final year of the Deshaun Watson contract. The albatross that has hung over the Browns head for five years could finally be behind them. There's an $86.2 million cap hit to deal with, but the Browns don't have to have him on the roster.

Watson's time in Cleveland has been tumultuous. The off-field issues, injuries and just flat out poor play have made him one of the worst investments in NFL history.

Yet, he's getting one more crack at getting his career back on track. He was named the starter of Shedeur Sanders which means he has the beginning of the season to prove that he's still a worthy starter in the NFL.

He's going to have to do it with a new head coach, new offensive system, a completely rebuilt offensive line and two rookie receivers who figure to play major roles.

He'll also have a second-year quarterback who went 3-4 as the starter last season.

That's a lot of pressure for a quarterback who has already alienated his team's fanbase with comments before the season even got started.

articles.title: 5 Buffalo Bills Under the Most Pressure Entering the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are broadly under pressure.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are broadly under pressure.

That's inevitable when you're the winningest regular-season team of the 2020s but have yet to reach a Super Bowl during that stretch.

That said, some players face far more specific pressure than others entering 2026.

The Pressure Point: The league's most valuable player since 2020 based on Pro Football Reference's AV metric is on a Hall of Fame track but has failed to get the Bills to the Super Bowl despite seven playoff appearances in a row. Now 30, Allen is facing considerable pressure to take that next step with this veteran team.

Best-Case Scenario: He stays healthy and puts together a seventh consecutive season deserving of MVP consideration and finally gets the Bills over the finish line. A Super Bowl loss would hurt but still represent progress for a guy with plenty of gas left in the tank.

Worst-Case Scenario: Any sort of regression in an offense that will have a fresh look with Joe Brady in the head-coaching role and Pete Carmichael joining the staff as offensive coordinator.

Prediction: The addition of top receiver DJ Moore and a new perspective from Carmichael help Allen finally lead the Bills to (at least) an AFC title.

The Pressure Point: Moore will be expected to validate Buffalo's decision to surrender a second-round pick for a highly paid 29-year-old who saw many of his numbers decline during his last two seasons with the Bears.

Best-Case Scenario: A new environment unlocks Moore and allows him to recapture the magic that powered four 1,100-plus-yard seasons in a five-year span between 2019 and 2023. As a result, Moore becomes the elite No. 1 boundary receiver Buffalo's offense needs.

Worst-Case Scenario: There's a lack of chemistry between Allen and Moore in a new offense, and the eight-year veteran continues his regression. It becomes apparent his career peaked a few years ago.

Prediction: He returns to the 1,000-yard club, and his talent and experience are crucial in big spots as the Bills make their Super Bowl run.

The Pressure Point: The winner of a critical summer battle to replace departed veteran David Edwards, Anderson will be the only new piece on Buffalo's offensive line. He's an undrafted 26-year-old with very limited pro experience, yet he won the job over the well-established Austin Corbett. As a result, the leash might not be long.

Best-Case Scenario: He uses his familiarity with Joe Brady's offense to become a reliable and consistent starter throughout the season. Perfection isn't required or expected, but it'd be nice if he could prevent the team from stressing about the left guard spot all season.

Worst-Case Scenario: He isn't ready for the task of blocking for a $330 million quarterback in an offense that has little margin for error, and the Bills are forced to pivot to alternative options on the fly this fall.

Prediction: The spotlight gets to him eventually, sparking a midseason debate on Anderson versus Corbett. The Bills rally behind Anderson and work with him to become a better player before the regular season is through, but it's another battle for a starting job in the 2027 offseason.

Late Additions Who Could Influence Super Bowl Hopes 💪

The Pressure Point: It appears to be a make-or-break contract year for a 25-year-old who has been more of a part-time player in his first three seasons but is expected to play a larger role as the team uses more 3-4 looks in Jim Leonhard's system. Shaq Thompson and Matt Milano are not on the 53-man roster but remain available if needed.

Best-Case Scenario: The 2023 third-round pick takes advantage of a philosophical defensive shift and wins over the new coaching staff with a breakout year, leading to a considerable payday in the 2027 offseason.

Worst-Case Scenario: He struggles in that heightened role and loses the starting spot, forcing the Bills to count on rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr and/or add back Thompson or Milano on the fly.

Prediction: Williams continues to excel in the run game but has some slip-ups in coverage, eventually leading to more of a platoon role with Elarms-Orr. The team moves on next offseason.

The Pressure Point: With Tre'Davious White off the roster (for now), the expectation is that Hairston will make a leap in his sophomore campaign. The 2025 first-round pick had a bumpy rookie year thanks in part to injuries, and now he's trying to hold on to a starting job that could be up for grabs if he struggles and/or rookie second-round pick Davison Igbinosun continues to impress.

Best-Case Scenario: Hairston makes steady progress in a healthy second season, and he and Christian Benford form an elite coverage duo by Thanksgiving.

Worst-Case Scenario: He once again proves unreliable over long stretches, causing the Bills to make changes in the secondary throughout the year.

Prediction: The 23-year-old shows occasional growing pains against premier receivers, but establishes himself as an above-average starting corner by January.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on C.J. Stroud's Leadership of Texans Amid Contract Buzz Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: Ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, there is reportedly a belief among those close to Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud that he is coming into his own.
articles.body:
Ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, there is reportedly a belief among those close to Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud that he is coming into his own.

According to Jeff Howe of The Athletic, people around Stroud feel he "made a jump as a leader this offseason," and that he "has taken more ownership of the offense."

Stroud, who turns 25 in October, is preparing to enter his fourth NFL season on the heels of going second overall in the 2023 NFL draft.

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

While Stroud is under contract through 2027 due to the fifth-year option in his rookie contract, there is little doubt that he will be seeking a new deal leading up to the 2027 campaign.

After his rookie season, it seemed like a virtual guarantee that Stroud was eventually going to become one of the highest-paid quarterbacks in the league.

He went 9-6 as the starter that season and led the Texans to a surprise AFC South title. He also threw for 4,108 yards, 23 touchdowns and just five interceptions en route to Pro Bowl and NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

Although Houston made it back to the playoffs in both 2024 and 2025, Stroud's individual play seemed to regress.

In 2024, he threw for 3,727 yards, 20 touchdowns and a career-high 12 interceptions, and he followed that up last season with a career-low 3,041 yards to go along with 19 touchdowns and eight picks.

The bigger issue for Stroud has been poor play in the playoffs over the past two seasons. In four postseason games in 2024 and 2025, Stroud went 2-2, completed 58.6 percent of his passes and threw for 989 yards, three touchdowns and six interceptions.

Five of those interceptions were thrown in last season's playoffs, including four in the Texans' AFC Divisional Round loss to the New England Patriots.

The Texans undoubtedly need more out of Stroud this season if they are going to take the next step forward and if they are going to make a massive commitment to him as the franchise quarterback for years to come.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last week that Stroud is likely to play out the 2026 season without a new contract despite the Texans being "prepared to put Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club."

Whether Stroud belongs in the group of quarterbacks making at least $50 million annually is very much up for debate, but he has a chance to remove any doubt with a bounce-back season in 2026.

The first step begins Sunday when the Texans host the Buffalo Bills in Week 1 of the regular season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce considered an $8 million investment in a $140 million golf project as Chiefs star expands his empire
articles.summary: NFL News: In 2024, Travis Kelce was already looking beyond the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end was reportedly exploring a major golf investment.
articles.body: In 2024, Travis Kelce was already looking beyond the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end was reportedly exploring a major golf investment that could become one of his biggest business moves yet. With an estimated $140 million project in the works, Kelce appeared ready to turn his growing interest in golf into a serious part of his long-term financial strategy.Travis Kelce plans $8 million investment in golf course projectAccording to an August 15, 2024 report from The U.S. Sun, Kelce was in talks to invest around $8 million in a group planning to develop and upgrade luxury golf courses across the United States, the Caribbean and Europe.The wider project was estimated at $140 million over five years. The plan reportedly included purchasing land for new courses while also modernizing existing properties and developing surrounding areas.The move made sense for Kelce, who had increasingly embraced golf away from the NFL. In July 2024, he played in the American Century Championship in Lake Tahoe alongside his brother Jason Kelce. He had also appeared in The Match in 2023 with Patrick Mahomes, Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson.A source close to Kelce's entourage described his growing business ambitions, saying:“Travis is turning into a serious and successful entrepreneur,” says one person close to Kelce’s entourage.“And he always has new ideas and is being approached by a lot of people and businessmen to join and invest in different fields, to extend his already very profitable portfolio.“He got approached not that long ago by a couple of people that own golf courses in many countries around the world, and he is really interested in joining them.”For Kelce, golf was reportedly about more than owning an asset. articles.title: Browns' Denzel Ward Purchases Guardians Minority Stake, Joins Travis Kelce, 'So Blessed'
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward is now part of the Cleveland Guardians' ownership group.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward is now part of the Cleveland Guardians' ownership group.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Ward purchased a minority stake in the franchise on the heels of Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce doing so in May.

Ward released a statement regarding his new involvement with the Guardians, saying, "Cleveland is my hometown. I'm so blessed to be able to show up for this city on the field and now as a part of the Guardians organization. I couldn't be more grateful to the Dolan family and David Blitzer for the opportunity to continue to pour into this community and give back to the best fans in the world."

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

The 29-year-old Ward was born in the Akron suburb of Macedonia, Ohio, he played his college football at Ohio State, and he has spent his entire NFL career in Cleveland after getting selected fourth overall by the Browns in the 2018 NFL draft.

Since entering the league, Ward has established himself as one of the top corners in the sport, earning five Pro Bowl selections and recording 18 interceptions and 104 passes defended over his eight NFL seasons.

Team success has proved elusive during Ward's tenure, though, as he has only reached the playoffs twice.

By comparison, the Guardians have been a playoff team in seven of the past 10 seasons and three of the past four.

They are currently in a battle for a playoff berth in the American League this season, leading the Toronto Blue Jays by one game for the final wild-card spot.

Expectations are not high for the Browns entering the 2026 NFL campaign, especially given their quarterback situation with Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, and after trading superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams.

However, with Ward joining the Guardians' ownership group under Paul Dolan and David Blitzer, he has a chance to win big this season, even if it doesn't happen on the football field.

articles.title: New Seahawks Rumors on Sam Darnold's Involvement in Brian Fleury's Hire as OC to Replace Kubiak
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks looped quarterback Sam Darnold into their process of hiring a new offensive coordinator, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks looped quarterback Sam Darnold into their process of hiring a new offensive coordinator, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson .

Henderson reported Wednesday that "Darnold was consulted during the search and supported" the choice of Brian Fleury to replace Klint Kubiak, who left to coach the Las Vegas Raiders.

The two-time Pro Bowler had some experience with Fleury thanks to his one season on the San Francisco 49ers in 2023. Fleury was the Niners' tight ends coach at the time.

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Since reuniting, Darnold found the coach is putting his stamp on the offense while carrying over "a lot of the same stuff" from Kubiak's scheme.

"Fleury obviously coming from San Francisco, but a couple different wrinkles here and there," he said in June . "So it's been good that way to be able to get some of that same verbiage but just a couple different wrinkles, like I said. So it's been really good to be able to get some stuff that he's been doing with San Francisco the last couple years and how we incorporate that into our system into what we've been building on the past year."

Given how important he is to the franchise, it made sense to ensure Darnold would be on the same page with a new offensive coordinator out of the gate. The veteran signal-caller obviously didn't make the final call, and Seattle may have hired Fleury anyway if Darnold wasn't totally on board. Why start things on the wrong foot, though?

It sounds like the transition to a different play-caller for the offense is going as well as fans could've hoped for.

articles.title: Clay Matthews’ jaw dropping transformation has NFL fans fooled - but there’s one huge problem

articles.body: Clay Matthews apparently got a new face, a new body, and possibly a new career as a Marvel villain, Thanos, or Hellboy.There’s just one problem: the NFL legend doesn’t look like the pictures circulating in cyberspace right now! The former Green Bay Packers linebacker became the far-fetched center of a cyberspace storm after images circulated showing him with a shocking new look.The pictures were dramatic enough to trigger instant speculation about plastic surgery, cosmetic procedures, and an extreme physical transformation - one that makes a particular feature stand out.Clay Matthews AI photos trigger NFL plastic surgery rumorsThe viral images appeared to show Clay Matthews looking almost unidentifiable, with specifically altered facial features and a more muscular physique - much like Hellboy, Thanos, or Hulk.The shocking images quickly became fodder for social media speculation about whether the former linebacker had undergone extensive cosmetic work.An X account called Former Republican subsequently warned that the images were AI-generated and a paid advertisement to “get people to listen to his crap podcast.” Clay Matthews’ brother, Kyle Matthews, runs “The Matthews Mentality” podcast.In its 100th episode, Kyle interviewed Clay about life after football, raising three kids, and working outdoors. He also recalls nearly taking a commercial real estate internship that Kyle arranged before choosing to pursue the NFL. Clay is also a guest on sports shows like Bussin’ With The Boys.As for the fake Clay picture, other reports also questioned its authenticity.Some compared him to several other characters, including Thor, Weaver from Antz, Handsome Squidward from SpongeBob SquarePants, Popeye, Crimson Chin, Joe Swanson from Family Guy, WWE superstar The Great Khali, Johnny Bravo, and internet creator Logan Chitwood, who portrays a “GigaChad” meme persona, among others.Clay Matthews plastic surgery claims face reality checkMatthews has largely stayed out of the NFL spotlight since his football playing career ended, making breathtaking “before-and-after” images peculiarly easy to believe for people who haven’t seen him recently.But recent appearances and footage reportedly show Matthews looking considerably closer to his familiar self. The one from his brother Kyle’s podcast in March 2026. Then the one from the 2025 NFL Draft. His latest appearance on the Bussin’ With The Boys podcast - dated Sept. 3.As for his actual football transformation? It was majestic enough.Matthews spent 10 seasons in the NFL, primarily with the Green Bay Packers. He became one of the most destructive defensive players of his era, earning six Pro Bowl selections and helping Green Bay win Super Bowl XLV.He finished his NFL career with 91.5 sacks, according to NFL statistics. Apparently, that resume wasn’t dramatic enough for cyberspace. They reportedly came with a distorted image! Now, by “they,” fans mean TMZ.NFL AI images prove just how easily fans can be fooledThis Clay Matthews episode highlights a bigger problem facing sports fans: seeing is no longer enough to believe.AI-generated images can produce convincing facial changes, physiques, and scenarios in seconds. Once those pictures are posted without context, speculation can quickly become “fact” through constant resharing. And Matthews’ case is almost comically perfect.A legendary linebacker known for his flowing blond hair and intimidating gridiron presence suddenly appears online, reportedly through TMZ, looking like he discovered an experimental NFL offseason program. Fans speculate. Social media reacts. Headlines follow.Then comes the inconvenient detail: the picture itself may not be authentic.Even fans went on to say, “I used to rely on TMZ for well-researched, accurate info until now,” and “I like TMZ because they post an event a full 5 minutes before it even happens, but I’m not sure what they are doing with this campaign of fake nonsense.”A post read, “Since when do you promote fake pics?” another said, “Why you so dumb TMZ! Desperate for clicks?”A user asked Grok, Twitter’s AI: “Hey [Grok], why is TMZ posting these fake pics of Clay Matthews with an oversized jaw?”Grok replied, “Modern AI-generated images can be virtually indistinguishable from real ones by sight alone. These of Clay Matthews are AI-generated, per community notes and multiple reports. TMZ posted them as promotional ads, and he joked “Gigaclay” about the exaggerated jaw and physique. No real work was done.”So before declaring that Clay Matthews has undergone the greatest transformation since his NFL debut, perhaps check whether Clay Matthews actually transformed at all.Because in 2026, apparently the most unbelievable thing about an NFL photograph isn’t always the athlete.Sometimes, it’s the photograph. articles.title: NFL Kickoff Game preview: Patriots try to be more competitive in Super Bowl rematch vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: The Seahawks' encore to their Super Bowl season starts on Wednesday in Seattle.
articles.body:
The NFL picking the New England Patriots as the opening game opponent for the Seattle Seahawks made sense, because it's a Super Bowl matchup.

It's also a little confusing, based on how that Super Bowl went.

For the most part we've had a run of competitive Super Bowls, but last postseason brought the second blowout in a row. The Patriots were overmatched from the start. The final score was 29-13 in favor of the Seahawks but it was even more of a mismatch than the score would indicate. The Seahawks defense suffocated the Patriots, who didn't score in the first three quarters. The Seahawks led 29-7 before a meaningless touchdown by New England in the final three minutes. Seattle outclassed New England in every way.

That doesn't mean a rematch will go the same way, however. The Patriots got better at receiver, signing Romeo Doubs and then making a big trade for A.J. Brown . The many players still on the roster since last season will remember being embarrassed in the Super Bowl and want to make amends for it. Though, they will be without a key player as running back TreVeyon Henderson is out due to an ankle injury.

The Seahawks have some motivation too. They've been an overlooked champion this offseason as their NFC West rival Los Angeles Rams take up all the attention with their big roster moves. The Seahawks have had some losses this offseason, most notably running back Kenneth Walker III and offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, but they were a dominant champion and won't take a backseat to the Rams.

"They made some big-time moves," Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba said on ESPN, via Heavy.com . "I think them getting Aaron Donald is great for them and we understand that. But like I said, we kind of don't care. We're gonna take these challenges head-on and we're excited about it, looking forward to it, and really just worried about us and what we have to do."

Each team has plenty of play for in the opener, which was moved to Wednesday night to accommodate Thursday night's 49ers-Rams game in Australia. Hopefully this game is better than the last time the Patriots and Seahawks met.

The Seahawks have the benefit of being the Super Bowl champion. If they aren't as good this season it will be disappointing, but they earned a pass for at least a season. The Patriots didn't get that Super Bowl, and the offseason was surprisingly harsh for a 14-3 AFC champion. Everyone enjoyed pointing out how soft the Patriots schedule was and explaining how they'd regress. A win at Seattle to open the season would change that narrative instantly. A team with Drake Maye at quarterback and Mike Vrabel at head coach, surrounded by plenty of talent including an upgraded receiver room, shouldn't be going anywhere for a while.

The Seahawks let Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, leave for the Chiefs in free agency. Part of the plan to replace him was drafting Price with the last pick of the first round. Many saw that pick as a reach, but Price is a talented player who happened to be behind Jeremiyah Love with Notre Dame. Zach Charbonnet is a capable back but he's out at least the first four games of the season as he recovers from a torn ACL. That means a team that likes to run the ball is going to rely heavily on Price through September. He has the ability to become a big factor beyond that too, if he shows he can thrive in a expanded role while Charbonnet is out.

The Super Bowl 60 rematch opened at Seahawks -3.5, but unlike the Super Bowl (which moved up to -5), the line has remained there and even ticked down to -3 at some books. Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez is no longer questionable with a contract dispute, as he'll suit up — while RB TreVeyon Henderson is out. Can Drake Maye look better against that Seattle defense? The Super Bowl champs haven't gotten much press this offseason, and they'll be waiting to take that out on New England on the field. The betting public likes Seattle to cover and I agree.

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

The Seahawks and Patriots kick off the 2026 season Wednesday night, a rematch of last year's non-competitive Super Bowl. Here are three fantasy angles to watch for:

Brown has been a consistent fantasy star despite spending seven years on teams that ran the ball into the ground. Drake Maye enters Brown's life at a perfect time, but the Patriots understand that Brown will need maintenance — he's dealing with a chronic, degenerative knee condition. Brown always made sense as a second-round fantasy pick this summer, but we also have some floor concerns.

2. Will Jadarian Price hit the ground running?

The Seahawks sure hope so, with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet unavailable for several weeks. Price might have been a slight reach as an NFL first-round pick, but he could approach 18-20 touches in the opener, given how ordinary the depth chart is behind him.

3. Have the Seahawks unlocked Rashid Shaheed ?

Seattle acquired Shaheed in the middle of the 2025 season and he did very little after the trade — a meager 15-188-0 line for nine games. But the organization still believes in Shaheed, giving him a three-year, $51 million extension after the season. Although receivers can sometimes produce quickly after a midseason trade (see Jakobi Meyers last year), slow onboarding is probably more common. We're eager to see if Shaheed can be a useful fantasy depth piece for 2026.

Hall of Famer Peyton Manning is returning to television screens this week, reprising his role as "Paintin' Manning" in Nationwide 's latest commercial.

"Bringing that message to life through 'Paintin' and Saquon gives us a distinctive, memorable way to help consumers understand how Nationwide helps them protect what matters today and plan for what comes next," Nationwide chief marketing and customer experience officer Ann Bair said in the release.

This is far from the first time Manning and Barkley have collaborated with Nationwide. The company has been an official sponsor of the NFL since 2014, and the two have respectively starred in several Nationwide commercials over the past couple years.

articles.title: Bills' Dalton Kincaid Talks Josh Allen, DJ Moore, NFL Super Bowl and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Take heart, Buffalo Bills fans. You aren't the only ones who dream of the franchise winning its first Super Bowl and the ensuing celebrations that would follow.
articles.body:
Take heart, Buffalo Bills fans. You aren't the only ones who dream of the franchise winning its first Super Bowl and the ensuing celebrations that would follow.

"It's something you think about," Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid told Bleacher Report. "I don't want to say frequently, but it absolutely comes to mind. Just the parade and everything. You can see it before it happens. It's something that drives and motivates a lot of people on this team."

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Few fanbases in all of professional sports have dealt with as much anguish as those of the Bills. After all, they infamously lost four straight Super Bowls from the 1990 campaign through the 1993 one and have fallen short of reaching the Super Bowl of late in each of their seven straight playoff appearances.

The 2020 and 2024 seasons ended with AFC Championship Game losses to the Kansas City Chiefs, and it was also Patrick Mahomes and Co. who eliminated Buffalo in the Divisional Round in the 2021 season when the Bills couldn't protect a lead with 13 seconds remaining.

But the thing about prolonged sports anguish is it makes it that much sweeter when a team finally breaks through and wins a title. Just ask Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs fans on the baseball side of things.

"That goal never changes," Kincaid said of lifting the Lombardi Trophy. "Everyone on our team plays for one reason and one reason only, and that's to bring a Super Bowl back to Buffalo. When we are able to do that, it's going to be awesome to celebrate with each other and our families, but also with the city of Buffalo because they've been through so much."

Buffalo has the quarterback to finally deliver that championship.

Josh Allen is arguably the best player in football with a resume that includes the 2024 league MVP, four Pro Bowl selections and four seasons with more than 4,000 passing yards. He completed 69.3 percent of his passes for 3,668 yards, 25 touchdowns and 10 interceptions to go with 579 yards and 14 scores on the ground last year and could be even better in 2026.

Allen's presence is the primary reason the Bills are on the short list of realistic Super Bowl contenders once again this season, but his overall importance to the franchise extends beyond the highlight plays.

"Just the energy he brings," Kincaid said when asked what Allen excels at that fans don't always necessarily see between the lines. "It's very rare to have a quarterback who is as skilled mentally and physically on the field as he is off it. Just the way he operates the locker room and can connect with everybody. And there's his competitive nature. That's probably his biggest strength. He wants to win at everything he does and be the best at everything he does."

Allen is going to have a new go-to target in 2026 after Buffalo added wide receiver DJ Moore from the Chicago Bears via trade.

While Khalil Shakir led the team with 719 receiving yards in 2025, no other Bills wide receiver even reached the 500-yard mark. They needed a new weapon in the aerial attack to fully unlock the offense, and they got just that in Moore.

He has four seasons with more than 1,000 receiving yards, can provide veteran leadership and has shown a knack for making the big play, such as when he caught game-winning touchdowns last season for the Bears against the rival Green Bay Packers first in the regular season in overtime and then again in the playoffs with fewer than two minutes remaining.

Moore's presence and the defensive attention he will draw should also create space in the middle of the field for the tight end combination of Kincaid and Dawson Knox.

"DJ is everything that has been advertised and more," Kincaid said. "Seeing the way he operates as a professional has been great. You don't always see that in vets who have had so much success. I feel like there are so many weapons on the offensive side of the ball, and it opens up everything to throw him in the mix. He can do it all, catch a short pass, catch a pass over the top of the defense. He can open up everything."

A new receiver was not the only major change in Buffalo.

The AFC East team fired head coach Sean McDermott after nine seasons, a 98-50 record and seven consecutive playoff appearances. It then promoted Joe Brady to head coach after three years of being the offensive coordinator, which just so happened to coincide with all of Kincaid's three seasons in the league.

The tight end is familiar with Brady's work as part of an offense that finished in the top 10 in the NFL in yards and points in each of those three seasons, including last year when it was fourth in each category.

"I'm a big fan of Joe's," Kincaid said. "Just the energy he brings, it's infectious to everyone on the team. The last few years I've felt that on the offensive side of the ball, but seeing the whole team come together as one with him is pretty cool. I'm excited to see how it goes. There will be adversity during the season like every season, but Joe knows that and is ready for that."

It may be a new position for Brady, but he is still the same around the team.

"Besides him celebrating when the defense makes plays in practice now, he's really the same guy," Kincaid added. "Which is exactly what you want and look for in this business. People who show up each and every day as the same person regardless of the ebbs and flows of the league."

Kincaid is also looking to show up each and every day this season for his team, which is one reason he partnered with Q-Collar.

Q-Collar is the only FDA-cleared sports equipment that helps protect the brain from repetitive impacts and is worn by the likes of Sauce Gardner, Kyren Williams, Dalton Schultz and more.

"I've worn the Q-Collar the past couple seasons," Kincaid said. "It helps me play my game knowing that I'm prioritizing my brain health while I'm out there. It's a very violent sport we play with a lot of collisions, and the Q-Collar brings a lot of peace of mind when I'm out there."

"What initially made me want to work with them was attending Tight End U my rookie year," he said. "Luke Kuechly is always out there, and they had a Q-Collar table set up. So I got to talk to him about it and saw he wore it previously. If someone the caliber of player of Luke Kuechly comes out wearing something like that, it holds some meaning."

Kincaid had high expectations entering that rookie year as a first-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft. While sharing a tight end room with Knox means he likely isn't going to consistently put up 1,000-plus receiving yards in a season, he has established himself as a key part of Buffalo's attack.

He also made his first career Pro Bowl last season behind 39 catches for 571 yards and five touchdowns.

"It was awesome," Kincaid said of the Pro Bowl nod. "It's cool to get that recognition and go and spend time with fellow teammates at those types of events. And I also got to meet other guys around the league and pick their brain. I got to know Tyler Warren pretty well and see what he does. Those experiences are so valuable."

At 26 years old and with three years of experience under his belt, it is reasonable to expect him to build on that first Pro Bowl appearance and take another leap in 2026.

"I have a few individual goals I write down and keep to myself, but the only real goal I have is winning a Super Bowl and winning a Super Bowl in Buffalo," Kincaid said.

Realizing that goal would set off a generational celebration.
